Although existing methods have made substantial progress in intra-domain TF forecasting, inter-domain TF forecasting remains underexplored and faces several fundamental challenges. Specifically, semantic gaps between technologies from different domains hinder effective representation learning; historical inter-domain TFs are highly sparse, limiting the ability to learn reliable structural dependencies; and intra-domain and inter-domain TFs exhibit distinct flow patterns, which are difficult to model within a unified framework. To address these challenges, in this paper, we propose an LLM-enhanced Graph Contrastive Learning (LGCL) framework that supports both intra-domain and inter-domain TF forecasting. Specifically, we first leverage LLMs with bias-aware representation adjustment to generate semantically enriched and accurate technology representations to bridge gaps across multiple domains. Then, to mitigate the sparsity of inter-domain TF data, a technology co-occurrence view is incorporated to complement historical TF information. We further develop a non-negative contrastive learning module to integrate the TF and co-occurrence views, enabling effective representation alignment without relying on negative samples. In addition, we design decoupled loss functions to separately supervise intra-domain and inter-domain flows, mitigating the difficulty of jointly modeling their different flow patterns under a unified objective. Finally, experiments on real-world datasets validate the effectiveness of our approach and provide valuable insights into future technology flow trends. Our code is available at https://github.com/huijieliu2023/LGCL.","already_present":false,"authors":["Hui-Jie Liu","Shu-Lan Ruan","Qian-Yi Cai","Qi Liu","Yu Liu","Hui Xiong","En-Hong Chen","You He"],"candidate_id":"candidate-6d728dd33b0c5a76616d6b1e","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"doi":"10.1145/3859876","semantic_scholar":"f9b146820dc7c06d510fb1d54423eed41ef0da02"},"identity_key":"doi:10.1145/3859876","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/f9b146820dc7c06d510fb1d54423eed41ef0da02","title":"LLM-enhanced Graph Contrastive Learning for Technology Flow Forecasting","venue":"ACM Transactions on Information Systems","year":2026},{"abstract":"Graph anomaly detection (GAD) aims to identify irregular entities in graph-structured data, yet heterogeneous anomaly patterns and distributional differences across graphs challenge generalizable detection. Existing training-free approaches avoid task-specific optimization but primarily rely on predefined numerical scoring rules, leaving the semantic interpretation of heterogeneous anomaly evidence largely unexplored. In this paper, we propose Jev-GAD, a training-free generalist graph anomaly detection framework that bridges heterogeneous numerical evidence and pretrained decision mechanisms. To address heterogeneous anomaly patterns, we construct complementary structural, attribute, and neighborhood evidence and transform heterogeneous statistics into graph-relative anomaly percentiles. To move beyond predefined numerical scoring rules, we leverage a single frozen pretrained language model for evidence-conditioned anomaly assessment. To bridge the semantic gap between numerical evidence and pretrained models, we design a semantic Graph-to-State (G2S) transformation that organizes graph context and semantically labeled node evidence into structured decision states for non-generative option-logit readout. The resulting decision scores are integrated with four complementary statistical scores through equal-weight rank-based fusion, without GAD-specific gradient-based optimization. a hybrid deep learning model with feature fusion attention and dual parallel CNN for drug-target binding affinity prediction","venue":"Journal of Supercomputing","year":2026},{"abstract":"Designing optimal auctions for allocating public infrastructure-such as airport slots and energy resources-is challenging due to interdependent resources and complex side-constraints. While the Vickrey-Clarke-Groves (VCG) auction guarantees maximum welfare, it cannot maximize revenue or accommodate the multi-objective trade-offs inherent in public infrastructure systems. We propose a differentiable, constraint-aware framework for combinatorial auction design that enables end-to-end learning of fractionally feasible, approximately strategy-proof mechanisms. Our primary contribution is a combinatorial constraint enforcement technique that ensures fractional feasibility by construction, bypassing the need for penalty-based approximations. We introduce CAGraph, a novel graph-based architecture designed to capture dependencies between items and bidders, alongside CANet and CAFormer as deep learning baselines, for combinatorial settings. We also provide a Matching Pursuit-inspired decomposition that maps fractional allocations to feasible discrete allocations and empirically evaluates the resulting discretization gap. In synthetic benchmarks and an airport slot-divestiture case study, respectively, the learned mechanisms achieve up to 73.5% and 180% higher expected revenue than VCG, under small empirical regret. Finally, we visualize the Pareto frontiers for revenue, welfare, and fairness, providing regulators with a decision-support tool to design infrastructure auctions that balance profitability, efficiency and equity.","already_present":false,"authors":["Mai Pham","Vikrant Vaze","Peter Chin"],"candidate_id":"candidate-c36c345925b43185b2f442af","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.31977","semantic_scholar":"eab9ee1087cb64d6ebec5e47a12bfa0f747940f7"},"identity_key":"arxiv:2610.31977","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/eab9ee1087cb64d6ebec5e47a12bfa0f747940f7","title":"Differentiable Combinatorial Auction Design: Optimizing Revenue-Welfare-Fairness Frontiers With Graph Attention Networks","venue":null,"year":2026},{"abstract":"Spatial multi‐omics technologies jointly profile multiple molecular layers in situ, enabling integrated characterization of tissue organization and cellular states. However, many graph-based approaches remain computationally demanding because they rely on repeated message passing over global graphs, whereas naive local sampling may disrupt cell-level correspondence when multimodal features and graph topologies are not induced synchronously. Moreover, simple concatenation or fixed-weight fusion does not explicitly account for unequal uncertainty between expression‐derived and spatial evidence, making the learned representations sensitive to feature corruption, technical noise and modality inconsistency.\n \n \n \n We present SubPoE, a subgraph-induced Product-of-Experts framework for spatial multi‐omics integration. SubPoE synchronously induces aligned local subgraphs from modality‐specific molecular similarity graphs and a shared spatial graph, preserving molecular‐similarity topology correspondence while reducing per‐iteration graph complexity. Dual‐topology variational graph encoders model expression-derived structure and spatial context as probabilistic experts, which are adaptively fused according to their uncertainty through a Product‐of‐Experts formulation. A composite self-supervised objective further improves robustness and cross‐modal alignment.\n \n \n \n Across eight public paired spatial multi‐omics datasets, SubPoE achieves competitive and comparatively stable performance against existing methods. Ablation, sensitivity, robustness and efficiency experiments further support the contributions of synchronous subgraph induction and uncertainty‐aware fusion.\n \n \n \n These results establish SubPoE as an effective approach for learning topology‐preserving, uncertainty-aware representations of heterogeneous spatial multi‐omics data.","already_present":false,"authors":["Yuan-Fang Li","Wen-Tao Gao","Jun-Hao-Ren-Jun-Hao Ren","Qian-Ran Wei","Xin-Lei Wang","Li-Heng Zhang","Rui-Ting Li","Ya-Dong Wang","Xiao Zhang"],"candidate_id":"candidate-2a65d261fc31cbcf6fdea292","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"doi":"10.3389/fgene.2026.1977260","semantic_scholar":"d85b33b5c685ef448d629eb4e1e07e7b4a569331"},"identity_key":"doi:10.3389/fgene.2026.1977260","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/d85b33b5c685ef448d629eb4e1e07e7b4a569331","title":"SubPoE: a subgraph-induced Product-of-Experts framework for spatial multi-omics integration","venue":"Frontiers in Genetics","year":2026},{"abstract":"Manufacturing operators must maintain production while limiting emissions when disturbances spread through shared resources. In contrast, analytical mixed-size placers optimize differentiable full netlist wirelength and density objectives but are typically unaware of thermal effects. An analytical placer acts as an online physical response model, exposing the standard cell distribution and a full netlist wirelength proxy induced by each intermediate macro placement, while a differentiable thermal model provides temperature feedback. Ablation studies further demonstrate that analytical and thermal guidance provide distinct and complementary benefits across wirelength proxies, routed wirelength, and thermal objectives.","already_present":false,"authors":["Qi Zhou","Guo-Jun Liu","Juan-Hong Zhao","Guang-Zhi Qi","Ze-Hao Chen","Ming Lu"],"candidate_id":"candidate-54364fca714eaf5998590140","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.33099","semantic_scholar":"e8641e4d155b54c7e617c48dd77b7efa73d1d3cf"},"identity_key":"arxiv:2610.33099","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/e8641e4d155b54c7e617c48dd77b7efa73d1d3cf","title":"EGGPlacer: Energy-Guided Generative Chip Placement with Diffusion Models","venue":null,"year":2026},{"abstract":"Protein classifiers are highly sensitive to evaluation protocol: random train/test splits induce phylogenetic leakage, allowing models to exploit taxon-specific correlations and substantially overestimate out-of-distribution performance. This issue is particularly acute for venom compound classification by ion-channel target (Ca2+, K+, Na+), where reported accuracies of 80-90% do not reflect generalization to unseen taxa. We formulate cross-species prediction as a structured distribution shift in which taxonomic identity acts as a confounder, requiring representations that capture structural features invariant across phylogeny. Using a shared multimodal backbone that fuses ESM-2 sequence embeddings with a disulfide-aware graph attention network, we systematically compare five structural inductive biases (spectral, Riemannian, SE(3)-invariant, statistical-manifold, and persistent-homology representations) under a leave-one-taxon-out evaluation protocol on a benchmark of 1,373 ColabFold-predicted venom compounds spanning five taxa. The persistent-homology representation summarizes backbone geometry through topological descriptors that are robust to local structural perturbations, providing an inductive bias toward phylogenetically invariant learning. Under conventional i.i.d. splits, all models achieve similar accuracy (81-86%), masking differences in inductive bias. Under taxonomic shift, this parity collapses: a sequence-only baseline drops to approximately 30%, the remaining geometric priors cluster at 54-55%, while our persistent-homology model (PH-GNN) achieves 63.4%, outperforming the next-best method by over 8 percentage points. Nevertheless, the current lane detection algorithms may face difficulties in complex driving situations due to poor visual feature extraction, unstable temporal prediction, and inadequate modeling of structural relations between lanes.\n \n \n \n In order to overcome these issues, this paper introduces the unified spatio-temporal graph learning approach that integrates spatial feature extraction, temporal context aggregation, uncertainty-driven graph formation, graph attention reasoning, and geometric optimization. A geometry-aware optimization strategy is further introduced to encourage smooth and physically consistent lane predictions. The framework was evaluated on the CULane test set using the proposed row-anchor-based lane-existence and localization evaluation.\n \n \n \n Experimental results show that the proposed GraphLane framework achieves a lane-existence precision of 0.9769, recall of 0.8990, F1-score of 0.9363, and an average localization error of 19.28 pixels. Although RAG and Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) provide practical ways to enhance LLMs, they remain insufficient for temporal reasoning. Existing retrieval methods typically prioritize semantic relevance while overlooking temporal validity, event order, and evolutionary dependencies, resulting in evidence that is relevant in isolation but temporally fragmented. Meanwhile, conventional PEFT methods usually employ fixed and input-agnostic low-rank updates, making it difficult to capture time-dependent entity semantics and relation drift. To address these limitations, we propose Temporal Evidence-Parameter Co-Alignment (TEPCA), a framework for LLM reasoning over TKGs. TEPCA aligns LLM reasoning with temporal knowledge at both the evidence and parameter levels. At the evidence level, it introduces time-constrained Dynamic Relevance-Guided Path (DRGP) pruning to preserve globally coherent temporal paths, together with Mutual-Information (MI)-based pruning to retain query-informative local facts under temporal constraints. At the parameter level, it integrates Dynamic-Gated LoRA (DG-LoRA), a timestamp-conditioned low-rank adaptation mechanism that dynamically modulates the effective adaptation subspace according to temporal context. This design enables LLMs to better capture fine-grained entity evolution and time-dependent relation semantics while preserving parameter efficiency. Experimental results on two TKG benchmarks demonstrate that TEPCA achieves state-of-the-art performance. Additional evaluations of DG-LoRA on eight commonsense QA datasets further verify its general input-adaptive capacity, scalability across LLM backbones, and interpretability.","already_present":false,"authors":["Jia-Pu Wang"],"candidate_id":"candidate-45c9d7646a18fd9444e79907","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.28176","semantic_scholar":"40365fb2fb2161e6bac5931c448e4bad3ae5971a"},"identity_key":"arxiv:2610.28176","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/40365fb2fb2161e6bac5931c448e4bad3ae5971a","title":"Temporal Evidence-Parameter Co-Alignment for LLM Reasoning over Temporal Knowledge Graphs","venue":null,"year":2026},{"abstract":"Autonomous mobile robots require spatial representations that capture geometry and semantics while staying sparse enough for planning in large, unknown environments. Graphs provide a natural representation for this purpose and underpin both classical planning methods and a growing class of reinforcement-learning (RL) policies. However, RL training needs hundreds to thousands of parallel environments, each constructing and updating its own graph. Existing graph libraries are typically designed for either single-robot deployment or fixed graphs, and CPU-based graph construction limits scalable training to only a few dozen environments. We introduce GGraph, an open-source GPU-accelerated graph library for both robot deployment and large-scale learning. GGraph supports real robots through ROS 2 interfaces and vectorized GPU-based policy training, with built-in support for tasks including 3-D navigation, exploration, and loop-closure integration. For single-robot operation, GGraph updates graphs in milliseconds. At scale, it enables graph-based exploration policies to train across hundreds of parallel robots, reducing wall-clock training time by one order of magnitude. Across simulation and real-world experiments, these results establish GGraph as a unified graph infrastructure for both large-scale robot learning and deployment.","already_present":false,"authors":["Yash Rampuria","Rohan Garg","Daniele Gammelli","Marco Pavone"],"candidate_id":"candidate-380ea401329575078d7ab866","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.28953","semantic_scholar":"62499a638974c7fdadc510b709ff14a595216de5"},"identity_key":"arxiv:2610.28953","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/62499a638974c7fdadc510b709ff14a595216de5","title":"GGraph: A GPU-Accelerated Library for Graph-Based Robot Deployment and Learning","venue":null,"year":2026},{"abstract":"Drug combination therapy has emerged as a promising strategy for improving therapeutic efficacy. While hypergraphs have demonstrated substantial potential for high-order drug synergy modeling, existing approaches still suffer from two critical limitations: (1) reliance on locally determined aggregation limits the utilization of multihop topological context and broader structural information across the hypergraph; (2) homogeneous message passing overlooks the structural heterogeneity of drugs and cell lines within hyperedges. To address these issues, we propose GLH2Syn, a global–local dual-view heterogeneous hypergraph learning framework for drug synergy prediction. Specifically, GLH2Syn operates on a heterogeneous hypergraph in which each drug–drug–cell line triplet forms a hyperedge, incorporating two complementary views: a global diffusion view and a local topology view. The global diffusion view performs diffusion over the node–hyperedge topology to derive globally informed incidence weights, thereby incorporating structural context into local aggregation. The local topology view captures fine-grained structural heterogeneity within hyperedges through structure-aware node-hyperedge propagation, distinguishing the heterogeneous roles of drugs and cell lines in high-order interactions. Furthermore, we design a joint optimization objective integrating drug synergy prediction with similarity reconstruction to preserve both predictive accuracy and biological consistency. Extensive experiments on two public data sets demonstrate that GLH2Syn consistently outperforms 11 competitive baselines on both classification and regression tasks across three test scenarios. Classical interior-point methods are robust and accurate, but their iterative nature can be costly in real-time or repeated-solve settings. This has motivated learning-based solvers that approximate optimizer solutions with neural networks. Rather than predicting the solution in a single pass, SOCPNet learns from intermediate iterates to progressively refine its estimates using a trajectory-regularized training procedure. We evaluate SOCPNet on multiple datasets spanning standard SOCP problem classes and show that it consistently reduces the final solution error relative to a SOCP-GNN baseline. Meanwhile, graph-structure order optimization is already NP-hard, and the additional KV-cache reuse objective further complicates the search by introducing potentially conflicting orders. However, existing methods face two key challenges when processing sports scenes: on one hand, target distribution in sports footage is strictly constrained by field boundaries, yet generic detectors uniformly allocate detection resources across the entire image, causing frequent false detections in off-field regions due to the visual similarity between spectators and athletes; on the other hand, objects such as athletes, balls, and referees in sports scenes form stable spatial co-occurrence patterns governed by game rules, yet existing methods predict each object independently, failing to leverage cross-category relational cues to assist the detection of difficult targets. Experimental results demonstrate that SportRGDET achieves significant performance improvements on multiple sports detection benchmark datasets, validating the effectiveness of scene prior and relation reasoning mechanisms in sports scene object detection.","already_present":false,"authors":["Qing-Ya Ouyang","Chao-Yi Su","Qing-Yuan Li"],"candidate_id":"candidate-01b4abd2637fe5dd49f47842","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"doi":"10.1371/journal.pone.0348924","semantic_scholar":"aba7360477948d813a54f2a6d84e6e56fbebafa2"},"identity_key":"doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0348924","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/aba7360477948d813a54f2a6d84e6e56fbebafa2","title":"SportRGDET: Scene prior and relation graph enhanced detection transformer for sports scenes","venue":"PLoS ONE","year":2026},{"abstract":"Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) have demonstrated exceptional performance on graph-structured data. However, their success heavily relies on the availability of clean labels, an assumption that often fails in real-world scenarios. We mathematically derive that label noise smooths this distribution, which inherently increases its entropy and severely decreases interclass distinguishability. To address this challenge, we propose Leave-one-out Entropy Node Screening (LENS), an end-to-end framework that identifies noisy nodes by measuring the reduction in neighborhood entropy when a specific node is removed. To embed superpixels, current encoders crop them to bounding boxes and then pad, resize, or mask them, so background or fill values can leak into the node features. This matters in practice, and especially in medical imaging, where a prediction should depend on the tissue and not on an arbitrary preprocessing choice: on BACH, changing only the fill of the masked region shifts the accuracy of frozen encoders by up to 6 percentage points, larger than the differences among the four best encoders under mean fill, and the preferred fill differs between datasets, so it cannot be fixed once and for all. We present TAN (Tissue-Aware Network), a compact convolutional encoder (0.41M parameters) that processes each superpixel at its native shape and extent and excludes background from every operation, which makes its embeddings exactly invariant to the fill by construction. Under identical masks and an identical graph classifier, TAN's accuracy on BACH is not significantly different from that of the 303M-parameter foundation model UNI (81.1% vs. 80.7-82.6%, depending on the fill), with ~740x fewer parameters, ~1,190x fewer FLOPs, and no pretraining. On BRACS, TAN is close to a ResNet18 trained under the same protocol and trails the histopathology foundation models. An ablation with TAN's architecture but standard processing of fill-padded crops shows that masking keeps accuracy similar (nominally higher on BACH, lower on BRACS, within noise) at less than half the FLOPs.","already_present":false,"authors":["Jan Herschel","A. von Gladiss"],"candidate_id":"candidate-982bfe400a683d3b22e684c2","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.23475","semantic_scholar":"886d28e9d078a546083945e7c9dc3196c9966cf7"},"identity_key":"arxiv:2610.23475","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/886d28e9d078a546083945e7c9dc3196c9966cf7","title":"TAN: A Size- and Form-Adaptive Masked-Convolution Encoder for Tissue Graphs","venue":null,"year":2026},{"abstract":"Train delay heterogeneity between service categories is well known but rarely characterized at large scale from operational data, and rarely used directly to drive the design of graph-based delay-propagation models. This study uses the real International Railway Network Dataset (IRD2025) – 2,678,291 operational records from 3,324 trains across 1,397 stations on the Italian railway network, January–June 2024 – to empirically characterize this delay heterogeneity and to motivate and evaluate a heterogeneous graph-based delay-prediction framework (HTW-STGN).\n \n \n \n Exploratory analysis is conducted on the full real IRD2025 dataset, rather than the smaller synthetic validation sample used in earlier work, to characterize delay heterogeneity across the seven Italian train service categories and to test the empirical assumptions – cross-category delay correlation, weather sensitivity and category-level delay ranking – that originally motivated the heterogeneous-edge design of HTW-STGN. HTW-STGN is implemented as a relation-aware graph-feature aggregation model, with heterogeneous edges (same-category/cross-category) grounded in real, physically observed infrastructure sharing and evaluated on a held-out June 2024 test set.\n \n \n \n Results confirm and correct earlier reported patterns: regional services (96.4% of all records) have lower delays than long-distance categories, the opposite of the result reported from the earlier synthetic sample; the weather effect is real but moderate rather than strongly multiplicative as earlier estimated; and cross-category delay correlation is consistently weak (r = −0.05 to 0.37) rather than the high correlation (up to 0.89) that had originally motivated the choice of heterogeneous graph edges. Only 4.6% of station-to-station links in the network are used by more than one train category, and this real infrastructure-sharing structure – rather than delay correlation – is used to root HTW-STGN's heterogeneous edges. This design reduces mean absolute delay-prediction error by 12% beyond a homogeneous-graph baseline (95% CI [0.49, 0.63] min, p < 0.001) and by approximately 40% beyond features that ignore graph structure entirely, consistently across all seven categories.\n \n \n \n This is the first large-scale empirical characterization of delay heterogeneity across the full real Italian Railway Network Dataset, and the first to test – and correct – the correlational assumptions behind a heterogeneous graph-based delay-propagation architecture using real operational data rather than a synthetic proxy. Graph neural networks (GNNs) rely on message passing over these edges, making relational privacy protection a critical concern. To mitigate privacy risks, edge-level differential privacy (DP) has been widely adopted to perturb graph structures. However, existing edge-level DP mechanisms apply uniform perturbation across all edges, disregarding their heterogeneous structural importance. To address this limitation, we propose a personalized edge-level privacy-preserving GNN (PELP-GNN) learning framework, the first personalized edge-level privacy-preserving GNN learning framework, whose key novelty is to assign each edge a differentiated privacy budget according to its structural significance, thereby avoiding the overprotection of low-importance edges and the underprotection of critical ones. Specifically, PELP-GNN estimates edge importance based on forest edge centrality (FEC) and allocates personalized privacy budgets accordingly. Furthermore, it incorporates an adaptive aggregation scheme to mitigate the effects of nonuniform noise during message passing. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that PELP-GNN satisfies $\\epsilon $ -edge local DP (LDP) while providing personalized protection. Unlike existing works, PELP-GNN is a general, plug-and-play framework that can be seamlessly integrated into state-of-the-art edge-level DP-based GNN learning frameworks. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in accuracy across varying privacy budgets.","already_present":false,"authors":["Zi-Jun Song","Dian Lei","Yan-Li Yuan","Lie-Huang Zhu"],"candidate_id":"candidate-23f5d8307d957e5da1d08b7c","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"doi":"10.1109/jiot.2026.3721975","semantic_scholar":"0dab363602973fe3d7a9d49f3f2f47a6dd9694e4"},"identity_key":"doi:10.1109/jiot.2026.3721975","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/0dab363602973fe3d7a9d49f3f2f47a6dd9694e4","title":"Achieving Personalized Edge-Level Privacy-Preserving Graph Neural Networks on Decentralized Graphs","venue":"IEEE Internet of Things Journal","year":2026},{"abstract":"Cooperative localization (CL) is a key enabler for future cooperative intelligent transportation system applications. By sharing and fusing multisource information, it can provide high-accuracy localization for connected autonomous vehicles in GNSS-denied or limited environments. Practical CL scenarios often involve heterogeneous cooperative nodes, such as vehicles and landmarks, and relative measurements (e.g., range and bearing). However, existing graph neural network (GNN)-based CL methods do not sufficiently account for scene heterogeneity or fully exploit relative information. Moreover, the state components estimated in CL exhibit substantial scale discrepancies, making effective joint optimization crucial for improving the overall estimation performance of the model. To address these issues, a heterogeneous CL Graph Transformer (HCLGT), together with an adaptive optimization strategy, is proposed for the real-vehicle CL task. First, we incorporate edge-based relative position encoding into the attention computation to better leverage relative measurements. Second, we design relation-specific aggregation modules for different measurement relationships and employ node uncertainty to adaptively adjust attention weights, improving robustness under heterogeneous information quality. Finally, an adaptive loss function is developed to dynamically balance the optimization of multiscale state components. The proposed method is validated on the real-world Leibniz University Cooperative Perception and Urban Navigation Dataset (LUCOOP). Experimental results show that, compared with the best-performing baseline, the proposed method reduces the localization RMSE by 44.61%. Extensive experimental analyses further validate the effectiveness of each module.","already_present":false,"authors":["Sheng-Sheng Xing","Hai-Gen Min","Xia Wu","Wu-Qi Wang","Xiang-Mo Zhao","Guo-Qiang Mao"],"candidate_id":"candidate-1759d0ab90fd511ada8523ff","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"doi":"10.1109/jiot.2026.3720786","semantic_scholar":"dc5cc46d1ade8958a153b1c27d278a58760b3dbe"},"identity_key":"doi:10.1109/jiot.2026.3720786","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/dc5cc46d1ade8958a153b1c27d278a58760b3dbe","title":"Heterogeneous Graph Transformer for Connected Autonomous Vehicles' Cooperative Localization","venue":"IEEE Internet of Things Journal","year":2026},{"abstract":"Longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs) contain complementary diagnostic and laboratory information about patient health. However, irregularity, sparsity, heterogeneity, and incompleteness in documentation complicate EHR modeling. To address the problem, we introduce GraphBEAT (Graph-based Bucketized Event Aggregation over Time), a temporal graph representation learning framework that groups clinical events into time buckets and transforms observed features into patient-specific, temporally directed graphs to enable early risk stratification for gastrointestinal cancers. Each node in an EHR graph encodes feature identity, observed value, and temporal position of clinical events. A context-aware, time-decay message-passing mechanism models transitions between successive buckets, followed by multi-head attention pooling to generate patient-level representations. GraphBEAT was trained and evaluated on multi-site longitudinal diagnosis codes and laboratory tests to predict pancreatic, liver, and intestinal cancer at 12-, 24-, and 36-month diagnostic lead times. In all experimental setups, GraphBEAT consistently outperformed baseline graph neural networks (GraphSAGE, GAT, and GCN) and sequence modeling approaches (Transformer and long short-term memory [LSTM]). GraphBEAT also required over 250x fewer floating-point operations per patient and over 20x fewer parameters than the Transformer and LSTM baselines. Their size, however, targets data-centre inference, whereas low-inertia operation increasingly asks for inference at the edge, next to the measurement, at batch size one and within a single synchrophasor (PMU) reporting frame. We distil a 20.1M-parameter, 12-layer GridFM teacher into a 0.62M-parameter, 6-layer student, a $32.5\\times$ parameter reduction at half the message-passing depth, using an objective that combines the masked power-flow loss with output, physics-residual, latent-state and attention transfer. The physics-residual term, which matches the teacher's power-residual profile, has not previously been applied to typed power-grid graphs. We evaluate on a renewable variant of the IEEE 118-bus benchmark grid in which 26 of the conventional (synchronous) generators are replaced by inverter-based renewables with battery flexibility and standardised reactive-power limits (IEEE 1547), giving $97\\,529$ physically valid (AC-OPF-feasible) operating scenarios, and we ablate all eight combinations of the transfer terms, reporting accuracy against ground truth and fidelity to the teacher separately. Distillation lowers student error on all four predicted quantities, by up to $48\\%$ on active-power dispatch, and every distilled student is more accurate than its teacher on reactive-power dispatch. The gain is largely carried by the output matching term. The physics-residual term, in the layer-aggregated form used here, is consistently harmful, which we attribute to the spatial averaging it applies to a bus-level residual field. The resulting student is $32.5\\times$ smaller in parameter count and has half the message-passing depth, making it a candidate for subsequent edge-device benchmarking.","already_present":false,"authors":["Vlad Sanduleac","Shahariya Rasheed Rayamarakkarveettil Puthanpurayil","Noman Khan","R. Teodorescu"],"candidate_id":"candidate-095ed2123891e867cce0baff","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.21833","semantic_scholar":"327773d82d16c35f9676a063b1c475fb8f49b7e0"},"identity_key":"arxiv:2610.21833","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/327773d82d16c35f9676a063b1c475fb8f49b7e0","title":"Physics-Aware Distillation of a Grid Foundation Model for Real-Time Edge Inference","venue":null,"year":2026},{"abstract":"Mobile apps have become ubiquitous in daily life. Despite communication encryption, app fingerprinting (AF) attacks can still enable adversaries to infer the apps in use by analyzing patterns of encrypted network traffic. However, existing AF attacks suffer from three critical limitations that hinder their practical effectiveness: (i) the inability to capture app-specific traffic dependencies, rendering traffic fingerprints fragile under dynamic networking conditions; (ii) the neglect of latency and throughput considerations, resulting in inefficient real-time user tracking; and (iii) the incapacity to handle mixed traffic generated by multi-app concurrency. In this paper, we propose MAppPrint, a robust and real-time app fingerprinting framework. MAppPrint introduces a behavior-level traffic fingerprint, i.e., Traffic Behavior Correlation Graph (TBCG), which models app traffic by capturing unit traffic behaviors and their correlations, thereby providing reliable app fingerprints. To enable real-time fingerprinting, MAppPrint incorporates a fingerprint compression algorithm that transforms each TBCG into a compact graph by selectively aggregating redundant information. Furthermore, MAppPrint employs an unsupervised decomposition strategy to disentangle mixed traffic generated by multi-app concurrency, enabling unified identification of both single-app and multi-app traffic. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that MAppPrint achieves 4.9~13.9% improvement in AF precision and 3~6 times improvement in timeliness over state-of-the-art methods. Meanwhile, MAppPrint is robust in dynamic networking conditions, while achieving a throughput of 10.5 GB/s and a prediction latency of 0.68 seconds.","already_present":false,"authors":["Tao Duan","Jun-Zhou Zhao","Jiang-Long Li","Rong-Hua Li","Youqian Zhang","Nuo Xu","Ping-Hui Wang","Hai-Bo Hu"],"candidate_id":"candidate-cad8432d4c0d3786b2b76f68","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.22148","semantic_scholar":"037546eb64d981ac1bc8401ea4d9fa524a7d3722"},"identity_key":"arxiv:2610.22148","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/037546eb64d981ac1bc8401ea4d9fa524a7d3722","title":"MAppPrint: Robust and Real-time Mobile App Fingerprinting via Traffic Behavior Correlation Graphs","venue":null,"year":2026},{"abstract":"Sheaf neural networks generalize graph neural networks by assigning each edge a learned linear restriction map that specifies how the local representations of adjacent nodes relate to one another, thereby mitigating oversmoothing. Existing sheaf architectures, however, define the sheaf Laplacian as an instantaneous spatial operator and therefore cannot explicitly model how signals evolve over time on a graph. We first introduce a spectral sheaf Laplacian, defined jointly over space and time, such that a single operator regulates signal propagation across both the spatial graph and the temporal domain. Directly extending this operator's receptive field in space or time would require increasingly complex sheaf structures. Instead, we propose a spectral filter that expands the effective receptive field along both dimensions without enlarging the underlying sheaf. Building on this operator, we introduce ChronoSheaf, a spatio-temporal sheaf network with two key components. First, Transitional Restriction Maps (TRM) decompose each node's restriction map into a spatial term and two temporal frames that independently control its relation to neighboring nodes at the preceding and following timestep, enabling asymmetric temporal influence. Second, the Dual Spectral Filter (DSF) applies a single bounded-degree polynomial filter with an adaptively estimated spectral radius to the joint spatio-temporal sheaf operator. We validate ChronoSheaf on a diverse set of spatio-temporal forecasting benchmarks, where it outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/ChronoSheaf-1D7D/.","already_present":false,"authors":["A. Mostafa","Zahra Ahmadi"],"candidate_id":"candidate-7dc9e4c88b61010b115dcc8e","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.21958","semantic_scholar":"b8986d71ee3df9284a0ce9362c22382bba11ffb4"},"identity_key":"arxiv:2610.21958","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/b8986d71ee3df9284a0ce9362c22382bba11ffb4","title":"ChronoSheaf: Joint Spatio-Temporal Spectral Filtering on Cellular Sheaves","venue":null,"year":2026},{"abstract":"The traditional performance cost accounting model of higher education shows obvious lag in dealing with the dynamic allocation of resources and multidimensional performance evaluation, so it is necessary to integrate data intelligence to improve accounting accuracy and management efficiency. Firstly, based on the data set related to education finance published by the Education Economics Laboratory, a heterogeneous graph modeling mechanism is designed to reconstruct the relationship between multiple node types, including teachers, courses, funds and outputs, and form a dynamic knowledge graph sequence. Secondly, by combining the Graph Attention Network (GAT) with the transformer architecture, a cross-time and cross-type performance cost representation model is constructed to support the teaching expenditure prediction and performance fitting analysis. Finally, an anomaly detection mechanism combining Autoencoder and Local Outlier Factor (AE + LOF) is introduced, and a closed-loop system is formed by optimizing budget allocation based on reinforcement learning strategy network. The results show that the prediction accuracy of the GAT model is better than that of the four baseline methods. In the annual scenario, the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) are reduced by 1.52% and 1.63% respectively, which has stronger error stability. However, recent studies have revealed their vulnerability to adversarial attacks, where imperceptible perturbations to the graph structure can easily mislead predictions. Existing defense methods predominantly rely on global heuristic strategies, which often lead to over-smoothing in deep architectures and fail to capture localized, fine-grained structural anomalies. In this paper, we propose Topology-Aware Dynamic Co-evolution (TADC), a novel framework that reformulates graph defense as a closed-loop optimization process. Unlike static purification paradigms, TADC introduces a closed-loop dynamic co-evolution framework, in which graph topology and model parameters are jointly optimized through validation-guided meta-gradients, enabling continuous and adaptive structural refinement during training. To further ensure the reliability of topology updates, we identify the topology-agnostic limitation of conventional meta-gradients and propose a topology-aware gradient calibration mechanism, which incorporates structural priors to guide gradient directions toward more plausible and semantically consistent graph modifications. Concretely, TADC first localizes vulnerable nodes via a structural-semantic consistency probe and constructs an initialized graph through topology-aware refinement. It then performs structure decoupling to disentangle reliable and potentially adversarial edges into distinct channels. Building upon this decomposition, a fully differentiable attention-based architecture DeepGCN enables end-to-end optimization of the co-evolution process. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that TADC consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across various attack settings, with particularly pronounced advantages under strong adversarial perturbations and high perturbation rates. Under the message-passing framework, mainstream GNN models alternate between feature transformation and neighborhood aggregation. Fusing these two phases into a node-level pipelined push dataflow, in which each node’s transformed feature streams directly into aggregation, establishes a single-pass I/O target that reads each input tensor exactly once per layer. No existing hardware sustains this dataflow at full concurrency. Prior fusion accelerators fall short of this target in three ways: designs that gather the raw input features for aggregation or write transformed features off-chip incur redundant traffic, designs that stream transformed features on-chip still keep the two phases as separate matrix kernels without a unified execution granularity, and the designs that aggregate at message granularity serialize per-destination aggregation or allocate state that does not scale to large graphs. We propose PipeGNN, a bandwidth-efficient GNN accelerator whose streaming microarchitecture sustains this dataflow as a fully concurrent pipeline within a fixed on-chip buffer budget. PipeGNN decouples execution from topological boundaries by aligning execution granularity with both memory burst size and aggregation compute throughput, and resolves four coupled microarchitectural barriers through coordinated mechanisms: compute-aligned edge batching, contention-aware message reduction, adaptive cross-batch scheduling, and tiered state residency. Evaluated across diverse GNN workloads, PipeGNN achieves geometric mean speedups of 10.1 × over AWB-GCN and 12.2 × over FlowGNN, and 2.4 × to 46.9 × over a GPU baseline across graph scales, reduces off-chip traffic by 2.69 × over AWB-GCN and 5.93 × over FlowGNN, and improves energy efficiency by 56.81 × over AWB-GCN and 1.53 × over FlowGNN, with a 154 × traffic reduction and a 116.81 × energy reduction against HyGCN.","already_present":false,"authors":["Shi Chen","Jun-Sheng Chang","Yang Guo","Li Shen"],"candidate_id":"candidate-382b7d011638e091c955c9dc","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"doi":"10.1145/3848033","semantic_scholar":"33f61137a3f7d187cda025344d3be520d557b091"},"identity_key":"doi:10.1145/3848033","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/33f61137a3f7d187cda025344d3be520d557b091","title":"PipeGNN: A Bandwidth-Efficient GNN Accelerator with Node-Level Pipelined Push Execution","venue":"ACM Transactions on Architecture and Code Optimization (TACO)","year":2026},{"abstract":"Subject indexing assigns descriptors from a controlled vocabulary to bibliographic records, a task characterized by thousands of labels, few positive examples per label, and a long tail of rarely used descriptors. Qualitative analysis shows the graph resolving errors that per-label scoring cannot, selecting a narrower gold descriptor where an unstructured re-ranker settles for its broader parent.","already_present":false,"authors":["Lakshmi Rajendram Bashyam"],"candidate_id":"candidate-9d56a14023cf9a9092fb212c","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.20048","doi":"10.1145/3805696.3846044","semantic_scholar":"2235eff7d497d10f077e66eb3b577e8a9b9eea7f"},"identity_key":"doi:10.1145/3805696.3846044","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/2235eff7d497d10f077e66eb3b577e8a9b9eea7f","title":"Reading the neighborhood: Text-Attentive Graph Reranking for Automated Subject Indexing","venue":"Proceedings of the 26th ACM/IEEE Joint Conference on Digital Libraries","year":2026},{"abstract":"With the widespread adoption of online social networks, social recommender systems have become a key paradigm for mitigating data sparsity and cold-start issues in traditional collaborative filtering. However, existing graph neural network (GNN) based recommendation models face two fundamental structural bottlenecks when dealing with real-world social data: social noise and over-smoothing. Invalid or weak social connections dilute preference signals, while representation homogenization induced by deep graph convolution undermines personalized recommendation. To address these challenges, this report proposes a new framework named SRIGB (Social Recommendation via Information Graph Bottleneck). Across observation spans and structural-record delays, true added connections achieve a 36%-50% reduction in mean true rank relative to the corresponding best baselines. This work provides a principled way to prioritize unrecorded additions for structural verification and record maintenance in online communities, information networks, and other networked systems.","already_present":false,"authors":["En Xu","Jing-Tao Ding","Yong Li"],"candidate_id":"candidate-69bd4315053b8ba0ec4c5593","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.16934","semantic_scholar":"5d78e27adf26560160f247d4d2fd66e51ce3c782"},"identity_key":"arxiv:2610.16934","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/5d78e27adf26560160f247d4d2fd66e51ce3c782","title":"Inferring Hidden Structural Changes from Node-State Responses under Partial Network Observations","venue":null,"year":2026},{"abstract":"Multimodal entity alignment (MMEA) is fundamental to integrating heterogeneous knowledge graphs (KGs), yet existing paradigms remain critically vulnerable to incomplete modalities and cross-graph structural asymmetries. This paper exposes a fundamental oversight in current MMEA research: treating feature missingness and topological discrepancies as isolated preprocessing or denoising challenges, which overlooks their destructive coupling during multimodal fusion. We systematically formulate and evaluate two newly identified failure modes: 1) Detail Missing (DM)-induced overvaluation, where the absence of local modality details causes models to overemphasize uninformative, blurred representations; and 2) Context Imbalance (CI)-induced suppression, where topological discrepancies across KGs allow dense structural contexts to overwhelm weaker but highly discriminative modal signals, triggering high-level semantic drift. To break this cycle of degradation, we introduce ALMEA, a generative and calibration framework that establishes a bidirectional feedback loop between low-level feature reconstruction and high-level latent space alignment. Specifically, Cross-Modality Imputation (CMI) synthesizes missing modality details to mitigate overvaluation, while Latent Semantic Calibration (LSC) aligns cross-graph joint embeddings to suppress topology-driven semantic drift. Under sparse supervision, we develop Controlled Iterative Selection (CIS) to adaptively acquire representative and diverse pseudo-labeled pairs, optimizing latent calibration under constrained budgets. Extensive evaluations on standard benchmarks demonstrate that ALMEA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. At a 20% supervision rate, ALMEA yields substantial absolute improvements of up to 5.20% in MRR and 6.40% in Hits@1, maintaining robust gains across higher supervision thresholds.","already_present":false,"authors":["Xi-Zhe Zhang","Jing-Feng Zhang","Meng-Fen Chiang"],"candidate_id":"candidate-6570ba1ef5a582d0637ec24c","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.16106","semantic_scholar":"283d12f5025036b5ad23089904fe5462312fdd48"},"identity_key":"arxiv:2610.16106","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/283d12f5025036b5ad23089904fe5462312fdd48","title":"Silence and Noise: Resolving Suppression and Overvaluation in Multimodal Entity Alignment","venue":null,"year":2026},{"abstract":"The global semiconductor industry has become a strategic pillar of the digital economy and mainly supports the artificial intelligence technology, cloud computing, advanced manufacturing, and modern electronic devices. However, cross‐integration of structurally unpaired and underutilized morphomic datasets (e.g., Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)‐stained images), remains a bottleneck due to inherent differences in spot structures, feature dimensions, and cellular heterogeneities. Here, we present AgaeSMO, an adaptive graph auto‐encoder for versatile cross‐modality integration of both structurally paired and unpaired spatial multi‐omics data. This paper proposes State-Intent-Aware Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Cooperative Driving under Imperfect V2X (SIGN-MAPPO) to address these challenges through three coordinated mechanisms. Each decision-eligible connected and automated vehicle (CAV) first reconstructs a receiver-specific traffic graph from its ego state and the peer-state records available to it, from which a shared graph-attention policy generates a raw Stop/Go intention augmented with predicted HV-intent features. CAV intentions are then exchanged through timestamped vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) messages, and a local conflict-aware arbitration layer converts each CAV's intention into a safe executable action despite potentially inconsistent peer information. In the principal Simulation of Urban MObility (SUMO) evaluation, SIGN-MAPPO achieves a 97.53% completion rate, a 0.10% collision rate, and a mean intersection traversal time of 35.28 s. Ablation studies further confirm the complementary contributions of HV-intent prediction and CAV-intent exchange to this performance. The trained policy also remains robust under the evaluated communication-delay and packet-loss ranges, and cross-scenario tests show complete traffic clearance across the tested settings, though safety margins narrow under compound unpredictable HV behavior.","already_present":false,"authors":["Zi-De Fan","Jia-Hui Yuan","Kai-Xin Zhang","Jun-Hao Fan","Xiao-He Li","Yi-Ru Wang"],"candidate_id":"candidate-0771915f54137e750f9afad9","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.15577","semantic_scholar":"f5a7931735282f7c2f40e19b26590d2cffae09e4"},"identity_key":"arxiv:2610.15577","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/f5a7931735282f7c2f40e19b26590d2cffae09e4","title":"SIGN-MAPPO: State-Intent-Aware Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Cooperative Driving under Imperfect V2X","venue":null,"year":2026},{"abstract":"In practical engineering and scientific computing, a real physical system can be reduced to a boundary value problem, and the adequate boundary information to determine the interior spatial distribution and evolutionary state of the physical field can be solved with linear equations, alternatively, the the real physical problem can be treated with boundary problems with in adequate information problems in field of machine learning. This paper proposes a deep learning framework for the recovery of missing boundary information using an attention-guided graph neural network (GNN) surrogate. The framework extracts features from the physical information on the discretized boundary into a latent space, and the missing boundary quantities are then predicted by the network. Thus, the nonlinear mapping from known boundary quantities to missing boundary quantities is learned using a variational autoencoder (VAE) architecture, while an attention mechanism is incorporated to better model the correlations among different types of boundary information. Furthermore, the interior physical field can be reconstructed using the conventional boundary element method (BEM) integral formulation. The effectiveness of the GNN-BEM framework is evaluated using numerical examples of the two-dimensional Laplace and Poisson equations, which demonstrate good performance in reconstruction accuracy, local detail preservation, and model stability. The results show that GNN-BEM provides a feasible computational framework for boundary information recovery and fast interior physical field reconstruction for partial differential equations under complex boundary conditions.","already_present":false,"authors":["Rong-Ze Gao","Yu-Wei Wu","Xin-Ran Ji","Xing-Yu Ren"],"candidate_id":"candidate-16757789a470e063a94a7b30","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.15590","semantic_scholar":"29a78d805053b7e62b05378613715df62e99efcc"},"identity_key":"arxiv:2610.15590","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/29a78d805053b7e62b05378613715df62e99efcc","title":"An Attention-Guided Graph Neural Network Surrogate for Boundary Integral Computation in Physical Field Reconstruction","venue":null,"year":2026},{"abstract":"Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown strong potential for text-attributed graph learning by leveraging rich pre-trained knowledge and language understanding capabilities. Combining LLMs with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) offers a promising paradigm for expanding the modeling capabilities of graph learning. However, LLMs and GNNs follow distinct learning paradigms, leading to a pronounced mismatch between their knowledge spaces. Such discrepancies make effective knowledge fusion nontrivial. To address these challenges, we propose DeKoR, an efficient framework for GNN and LLM knowledge fusion. We formulate this as seed-conditioned response ranking: given a perturbation at one seed node, ranking all other nodes by response strength. This is challenging when the model is given only the interaction topology, while the mechanism governing how perturbations propagate must be learned from data. We present VQIL (Visible Quantum Interference Learning), a trainable Szegedy quantum walk for seed-conditioned ranking. Edge weights, link phases, and per-node phase rotations are optimized end-to-end by backpropagation while the walk operator remains unitary throughout training. Node scores are obtained from a geometrically discounted coherent sum of quantum-walk amplitudes, enabling quantum interference before the final squared-norm readout. Because each learned parameter is attached to a named edge or node, the trained model provides directly inspectable hypotheses about the roles of individual graph components in the propagation mechanism. On AC power-flow perturbations over six transmission grids, with electrical parameters withheld from the model, VQIL improves Spearman rank correlation from 0.147 for the untrained walk to 0.831 and outperforms an identically trained random-walk model. On gene perturbation over five protein-protein interaction networks with Perturb-seq supervision, VQIL improves rank correlation from 0.171 to 0.620, outperforming the strongest learned classical and neural baselines. The hazard level of urban patrol cases can be reflected by the urgency level and prioritizing high-urgency cases can help reduce potential risks to public safety. However, it remains challenging to assess the urgency level of urban patrol cases when reliable urgency labels are limited or unavailable. To address this problem, this paper proposes an urban patrol case urgency classification method based on self-supervised clustering of a graph neural network. Experiments on the MAP-M2UAV50 dataset show that AMGT achieves high accuracy and efficiency. candidates.abstract: With the development of the integration of aerial, terrestrial, and satellite networks, Uncrewed Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) serve as a new type of aerial communication platform, playing a key role in Internet of Things (IoT) scenarios. However, multi-hop UAV networks still suffer from energy limits, bandwidth scarcity, dynamic topology, and unstable links. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an edge-cloud communication protocol framework (EC-LLM-MARL) based on Large Language Models (LLMs) and MARL. In this framework, the cloud side constructs a chain-of-thought to guide LLM reasoning, and distilled expert strategies are transferred to UAVs through knowledge distillation and fine-tuning, improving training efficiency and reducing communication overhead. Additionally, a Graph Attention Network (GAT) is employed to extract deep features of observation targets, while Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG) is combined with a self-attention mechanism at the UAV end to enhance credit assignment and convergence efficiency in dynamic environments. Furthermore, the framework designs a differentiated reward mechanism for task load balancing among multiple UAVs, improving the scalability of the algorithm in large-scale network scenarios. Extensive simulations show that EC-LLM-MARL significantly accelerates training convergence and substantially outperforms existing methods, achieving a 77% increase in throughput, a 13% rise in coverage, and the highest remaining energy levels.
candidates.title: LLM-Enhanced MARL for Multi-Hop UAV Networking: An Edge-Cloud Protocol Aware Framework

candidates.abstract: Person Re-IDentification (ReID) is vital for public-safety applications, yet camera-based ReID suffers in low-light environments and poses serious visual privacy risks. In contrast, millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar sensing has gained significant attention in ReID due to its ability to perceive human movement patterns by emitting electromagnetic waves, making ReID unaffected by lighting conditions and capable of privacy preserving. However, current radar-based ReID methods are primarily supervised, and radar data is challenging for human eyes to interpret, making annotation extremely difficult and costly. To this end, we propose an unsupervised radar ReID method based on multi-level cross-view mutual signal contrastive learning. First, to drive unsupervised contrastive learning that depends on data augmentations, we utilize signal processing techniques to transform raw radar signals into frequency spectrum and point clouds, and these forms constitute different and complementary augmented versions of the same sample. Second, we construct a multi-level contrastive model between frequency spectrum signals and point clouds through global contrast, cross-view prediction contrast, clustering contrast, and cross-view cluster center contrast, effectively aligning different views and enhancing unsupervised robustness. Additionally, we employ a well-designed local and global graph attention network to learn more discriminative radar point cloud features. Extensive experimental results illustrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing radar-based unsupervised methods.
candidates.title: mmWave Radar-Based Unsupervised Person ReID via Multi-Level Mutual Signal Contrastive Learning

candidates.abstract: With the rapid advancement of mobile technology and ubiquitous computing, spatial crowdsourcing has emerged as a promising computing paradigm. The growing complexity of spatial tasks has increasingly driven the demand for coordination among interdependent tasks and the cooperative participation of mobile workers, which remains relatively unexplored among existing studies. To fill this gap, this paper introduces Dependency-Cooperative Spatial Crowdsourcing (DCSC), a novel problem that explicitly models task dependencies and enables systematic worker cooperation to address complex spatial scenarios. To solve DCSC, we propose a two-stage solution: Dependency-aware Recommendation and Cooperation-aware Matching. In the first stage, we develop a multi-agent reinforcement learning approach enhanced with meta-gradient techniques to recommend suitable subtasks while considering dependency constraints. In the second stage, we propose a genetic algorithm-enhanced game approach to achieve optimal cooperative assignment, guided by a multi-dimensional matching utility function. To ensure consistency and optimization across both stages, we employ meta-gradients from the policy network to guide the optimization of the utility function. Additionally, we utilize graph neural network-based policy clustering to address task heterogeneity, enabling each cluster to learn specialized parameters and enhance reinforcement learning performance. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of our approach.
candidates.title: Efficient Task Assignment in Dependency-Cooperative Spatial Crowdsourcing

candidates.abstract: Addressing distribution shifts between training and testing sets is paramount for Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). Graph rationale learning has emerged as an effective paradigm to tackle this challenge by extracting invariant subgraphs as rationales for prediction. However, existing methods typically rely on the subgraphs produced by a rationale extractor without explicitly assessing their reliability, particularly during early training stages when the extractor is prone to generating inaccurate or biased rationales. Learning with such unreliable rationales can mislead the classifier and further deteriorate rationale quality, ultimately undermining generalization performance. In this paper, we rethink the objective of graph rationale learning and propose Cooperative Rationale Selection (CoRas), a novel architecture designed to enhance the reliability and robustness of rationale representations. Specifically, CoRas employs a dual-classifier framework to cooperatively select reliable rationales. Motivated by the small-loss criterion, CoRas prioritizes rationales with low prediction loss, while simultaneously selecting rationales with high prediction divergence to mitigate selection bias caused by relying solely on self-predictions during training. This allows CoRas to effectively select reliable rationales for downstream tasks, subsequently enhancing graph rationale learning. Experimental results on both real-world benchmarks and synthetic datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of CoRas in extracting reliable rationale subgraphs for combating out-of-distribution graph settings in graph classification.
candidates.title: CoRas: Cooperative Rationale Selection for Graph Rationale Learning in Out-of-Distribution Graphs
candidates.venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering

candidates.abstract: Modern power grids are increasingly exposed to diverse cyber-physical attacks that originate in the cyber layer and disrupt physical operation. A critical defense challenge is to rapidly determine whether an attack has occurred and identify its type. To address this challenge, this paper aims to develop a generalized detection scheme capable of identifying multiple types of attacks, particularly unknown ones. It is first observed that, under normal operation, cyber-layer data and physical-layer states are consistent across layers and evolve smoothly over time, while attacks disrupt these consistencies. Building on this insight, a self-supervised Cross-Layer Cross-Temporal Contrastive Learning (CL-CTCL) framework is proposed, which employs a Graph Attention Network-Gated Recurrent Unit (GAT-GRU) encoder to capture spatial dependencies and temporal dynamics. Two complementary contrastive objectives are introduced: Variance-Invariance-Covariance Regularization (VICReg) for cross-layer alignment and Information Noise-Contrastive Estimation with Momentum Contrast (InfoNCE-MoCo) for temporal consistency. Residual deviations from these consistencies provide reliable attack fingerprints, enabling detection and classification of both known and unknown attacks. Experiments on an IEEE 118-bus cyber-physical testbed show that the proposed CL-CTCL achieves high accuracy on known attacks and generalizes well to unknown ones, outperforming baseline methods across standard metrics.
candidates.title: Detection of Unknown Attack in Cyber–Physical Power Systems via Self-Supervised Cross-Layer and Cross-Temporal Consistency

candidates.abstract: Deep learning (DL)-based methods have illustrated excellent performance in distribution network fault diagnosis. However, the “opaque” nature of DL models hinders grid operators from understanding the decision-making processes of these models, affecting model trustworthiness and robustness in diversified diagnosis applications. This paper proposes a hybrid attention-augmented self-interpretable channel-grouped graph convolutional network (HASIG) for diverse short-circuit fault diagnosis of distribution networks, including binary fault detection, faulted line identification, and fault type classification. A channel-grouped graph convolutional network is proposed to learn features from three-phase voltage and current measurements. We present a hybrid attention that combines global edge attention and channel-grouped attention, which can augment the critical features with faithful and robust interpretations during model training, enabling users to gain insights into the predictive behavior inside the model. These three short-circuit fault diagnosis tasks are collaboratively trained under a multi-task learning architecture with interpretable loss constraints. Experiments were conducted on the IEEE 33-bus, IEEE 33-bus with distributed energy resources, and IEEE 123-bus systems with randomized fault parameters. The results show that HASIG achieves competitive diagnostic performance and good interpretability, and demonstrates strong robustness under noisy and missing-data conditions.
candidates.title: Hybrid Attention-Augmented Self-Interpretable Channel-Grouped Graph Convolutional Network for Robust Distribution Network Fault Diagnosis

candidates.abstract: This work addresses a fundamental challenge in applying deep learning to network topology-dependent power system applications: developing neural network models that transfer across significant system changes, including networks with entirely different topologies and dimensionalities, without requiring training data from unseen reconfigurations. We focus on situational awareness tasks where predictions inherently depend on network-wide spatial relationships through electrical connectivity. Despite extensive research, most ML-based approaches remain system-specific, limiting real-world deployment. This limitation stems from a dual barrier. First, topology changes shift feature distributions and alter input dimensions due to power flow physics. Second, reconfigurations redefine output semantics and dimensionality, requiring models to handle configuration-specific outputs while maintaining transferable feature extraction. Our core insight is treating topology as a learnable dimension through training on diverse reconfigurations, enabling the model to learn universal power flow physics rather than memorizing fixed networks. We achieve this through three synergistic mechanisms: scalar-weight graph convolutions with physics-aware operators handle variable input dimensions and distribution shifts, adaptive pooling maps topology-specific features to unified latent representations, and parallel transformer generates configuration-specific outputs using positional encoding. Our Universal Graph Convolutional Network (UGCN) achieves transferability to any reconfiguration or variation of existing power systems without any prior knowledge of new grid topologies or retraining during implementation. Experimental results on state forecasting and false data injection detection demonstrate that UGCN significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in cross-system zero-shot transferability across both transmission and distribution networks.
candidates.title: Universal Graph Convolutional Network: Zero-Shot Transfer Across Power Grid Topology Reconfigurations

candidates.abstract: Graph-structured representations of text data have become foundational across machine learning, yet it remains unclear how to systematically construct a graph from a given dataset for a target task. Choices about which entities become nodes, which relationships become edges, and what text each node contains can substantially affect downstream performance. In practice, finding optimal constructions often requires expert knowledge or manual trial and error. We introduce TACO-Graph, a decision tree framework for learning which graph construction choices are most effective for a given dataset and task. Specifically, we focus on text-attributed graphs (TAGs) constructed from multi-attribute tabular data. TACO-Graph enumerates valid TAG representations, scores each using fast proxy evaluation on small representative subsets, and trains an interpretable decision tree on those scores. Across five datasets spanning citation networks, product reviews, and bibliographic relationships, our decision trees predict construction quality on separately drawn evaluation samples with mean Spearman $\rho$ above $0.9$ for node classification and above $0.8$ for GraphRAG retrieval. Our trees systematically identify which constructions perform better across both GNN and GraphRAG tasks, and the full pipeline is released as an open-source library to support evaluation on new tasks and datasets at https://github.com/AmiriHayes/text_attributed_graphs. TACO-Graph provides a systematic and interpretable guide for determining how to convert tabular data to text-attributed graphs for downstream tasks.
candidates.title: TACO-Graph: Automated Construction of Text-Atributed Graphs

candidates.abstract: The realm of high-performance computing has expanded to include machine learning tasks of many forms. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are becoming increasingly popular, with their applications expanding across diverse domains. As the scale of graph data continues to grow, including larger numbers of nodes, edges, and higher embedding dimensions, standardized libraries such as DGL and PyG have been developed to facilitate GNN computation. These libraries allow the computation to be described a a high level of abstraction, providing high productivity on the part of the developer. However, with the rapid increase in the number of processor cores and the evolution of multicore architectures, these libraries often show poor scalability and fail to execute GNN inference efficiently on the latest multicore systems, particularly those with upwards of a hundred cores. To address this limitation, we introduce FrontGI, a fast and scalable set of techniques that advances the frontier of GNN inference on large-scale graphs (over 100,000 vertices) by leveraging graph-property- and architecture-aware design. FrontGI employs different parallelization strategies optimized for diverse graph structures, maximizing the utilization of multi-level cache hierarchies in multicore systems. We evaluate a number of GNN models with FrontGI on a 128-core AMD EPYC system. Compared to state-of-the-art libraries, FrontGI achieves up to 3.35$\times$, 3.20$\times$, 2.89$\times$ and 3.10$\times$ speedups over DGL for GCN, GraphSAGE, GIN, and SGC models, respectively, and even greater improvements over PyG, across a range of large-scale, high-dimensional graph datasets with diverse structural properties.
candidates.title: FrontGI: Architecture-Aware Parallel GNN Inference on Chiplet-Based Multicore Systems

candidates.abstract: A graph neural network (GNN) forecasting a collection of load series combines two mechanisms, sharing parameters across series and reading neighboring series, and a gain over a non-graph model may come from either; telling them apart decides whether a graph is worth maintaining. We propose a model diagnostic protocol that compares the GNN with three reference models: a per-node network, a network shared across nodes without neighbors, and the same GNN without edges. Degree-preserving rewiring tests whether neighbor identity matters. After a tuned benchmark on regional load in France and on low-voltage feeders in the UK, we apply the protocol to deliberately short node histories, as when non-stationary demand leaves only recent observations relevant: the feeders, within one week, and a public dataset of client consumption series. On the feeders, sharing parameters recovers most of the error gap between node-specific models and GNNs, about two thirds against a regularized one. Adding the edges to an otherwise identical backbone brings a smaller gain, half or more of which disappears under rewiring. On the client series, the neighbor mean degrades the per-node model on the shorter window and the edges'gain is not consistently distinguishable from zero; on the regions of France, where each node's own history is already informative, the ranking between per-node models and GNNs changes with tuning. A synthetic study points to noisy local measurements as one regime where neighbors help. In an exploratory online aggregation, graph and non-graph forecasters appear complementary, and the weight assigned to GNNs is not proportional to their contribution. In none of the three datasets do the edges account for most of a GNN's advantage over node-specific models, so a forecasting gain should be credited to the graph only after comparison with per-node and shared references.
candidates.title: A Diagnostic Protocol for GNNs in Electricity Load Forecasting: Separating Parameter Sharing from Neighborhood Access

candidates.abstract: Illicit account detection is a critical task for financial risk control systems, aiming to pinpoint malicious actors within transaction networks. Existing efforts typically recast transaction networks into directed multigraphs and leverage graph neural networks (GNNs) to detect anomalies via topological structures under the homophily assumption. However, directly grafting GNNs onto transaction graphs is faced with at least two pivotal challenges, i.e., structural inconsistency and label scarcity. The former arises from deceptive connections forged by malicious actors, while the latter stems from the lack of annotated data. In light of these, we introduce MINT, a novel graph neural framework that mitigates structural inconsistency via an attentive message-passing scheme on transaction graphs. Specifically, MINT introduces a discrepancy-aware feature propagation, which tracks malicious actors by quantifying deviations between nodes across bi-directional transaction flows. A transaction salience module is proposed to mitigate structural inconsistency by adaptively regularizing the interaction strength between nodes. Furthermore, to alleviate label scarcity, MINT is optimized via Positive-Unlabeled (PU) learning, which exploits only a minority of illicit nodes coupled with a majority of unlabeled ones. Extensive experiments conducted on three financial transaction benchmarks, including two large-scale public and one in-house real-world datasets, validate the superior effectiveness of MINT over several cutting-edge baselines.
