This study proposes a physics-guided framework that integrates a physics-informed Wasserstein generative adversarial network with gradient penalty (PIL-WGAN-GP), a dual-exploration spatiotemporal graph neural network (DEST-GNN), and an arbitrary-quantile recurrent decoder (AQ-RNN). The imputation module combines self-supervised masking, solar geometry, a clear-sky-based power envelope, and deterministic projection. The forecasting module fuses a static spatial prior with a time-varying dependency graph, while the decoder predicts aggregate PV quantiles directly through bounded positive spacings and monotone interpolation. The framework was evaluated in a retrospective case study using hourly PV generation records from 11 Belgian regional PV zones and matched meteorological records in 2025. For 3-, 6-, and 12-h consecutive gaps, PIL-WGAN-GP reduced normalized mean absolute error from 1.450%, 2.473%, and 5.252% for linear interpolation to 0.869%, 1.027%, and 1.300%, respectively. Hard projection eliminated nighttime leakage and upper-envelope violations. Across 1-, 6-, 12-, and 24-h horizons, DEST-GNN-AQ reduced the average daylight nMAE from 3.689% for the no-graph AQ-RNN to 3.509%, with the main gains occurring at 6–24 h. The model generated nested 50%, 70%, 80%, and 90% prediction intervals with a zero quantile-crossing rate. Their empirical coverages were 41.72%, 62.81%, 69.84%, and 85.26%, indicating that structural validity was achieved while calibration remains improvable. Collectively, these findings validate the proposed framework’s ability to bridge physically admissible data reconstruction with reliable, non-crossing probabilistic forecasting for PV clusters.","already_present":false,"authors":["Zhi-Hai Yan","Tian-Yu Xu","Zhong-Kai Shen","Wei Wei","Yu-Hang Huang","Jing-Xuan Long"],"candidate_id":"candidate-5812b67bbf139cddc8054bc8","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"doi":"10.3389/fenrg.2026.1952891","semantic_scholar":"411acacdece47cf233ed0d64d209a1a12949bb0f"},"identity_key":"doi:10.3389/fenrg.2026.1952891","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/411acacdece47cf233ed0d64d209a1a12949bb0f","title":"Physics-guided non-crossing probabilistic forecasting for distributed photovoltaic clusters using dynamic graph attention","venue":"Frontiers in Energy Research","year":2026},{"abstract":"This study focuses on the spatiotemporal prediction of supply chain finance risk contagion and constructs a model based on the dynamic graph attention diffusion mechanism for in-depth exploration. The risk-aware dynamic graph attention network (DyGAT) is used to model the time-varying network structure of supply chain finance, where the spatial attention weight α_ij(t) is updated adaptively at each time step by integrating real-time risk intensity signals to realize real spatiotemporal coupling modeling. A bounded diffusion mechanism with natural risk attenuation is introduced to characterize the propagation process of risks in spatial and temporal dimensions, avoiding unbounded cumulative defects in traditional formulas. Methodologically, a supply chain finance dynamic graph structure is constructed by integrating multisource data such as historical transaction data and corporate financial information, with clear data cleaning, fusion and feature engineering processes, and the model is trained, validated and ablated strictly. It provides strong support for financial institutions and supply chain enterprises to formulate risk prevention strategies in advance and is of great significance for improving the stability and resilience of the supply chain finance system. Although existing methods have made substantial progress in intra-domain TF forecasting, inter-domain TF forecasting remains underexplored and faces several fundamental challenges. Specifically, semantic gaps between technologies from different domains hinder effective representation learning; historical inter-domain TFs are highly sparse, limiting the ability to learn reliable structural dependencies; and intra-domain and inter-domain TFs exhibit distinct flow patterns, which are difficult to model within a unified framework. To address these challenges, in this paper, we propose an LLM-enhanced Graph Contrastive Learning (LGCL) framework that supports both intra-domain and inter-domain TF forecasting. Specifically, we first leverage LLMs with bias-aware representation adjustment to generate semantically enriched and accurate technology representations to bridge gaps across multiple domains. Then, to mitigate the sparsity of inter-domain TF data, a technology co-occurrence view is incorporated to complement historical TF information. We further develop a non-negative contrastive learning module to integrate the TF and co-occurrence views, enabling effective representation alignment without relying on negative samples. In addition, we design decoupled loss functions to separately supervise intra-domain and inter-domain flows, mitigating the difficulty of jointly modeling their different flow patterns under a unified objective. Finally, experiments on real-world datasets validate the effectiveness of our approach and provide valuable insights into future technology flow trends. Our code is available at https://github.com/huijieliu2023/LGCL.","already_present":false,"authors":["Hui-Jie Liu","Shu-Lan Ruan","Qian-Yi Cai","Qi Liu","Yu Liu","Hui Xiong","En-Hong Chen","You He"],"candidate_id":"candidate-6d728dd33b0c5a76616d6b1e","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"doi":"10.1145/3859876","semantic_scholar":"f9b146820dc7c06d510fb1d54423eed41ef0da02"},"identity_key":"doi:10.1145/3859876","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/f9b146820dc7c06d510fb1d54423eed41ef0da02","title":"LLM-enhanced Graph Contrastive Learning for Technology Flow Forecasting","venue":"ACM Transactions on Information Systems","year":2026},{"abstract":"Graph anomaly detection (GAD) aims to identify irregular entities in graph-structured data, yet heterogeneous anomaly patterns and distributional differences across graphs challenge generalizable detection. Existing training-free approaches avoid task-specific optimization but primarily rely on predefined numerical scoring rules, leaving the semantic interpretation of heterogeneous anomaly evidence largely unexplored. In this paper, we propose Jev-GAD, a training-free generalist graph anomaly detection framework that bridges heterogeneous numerical evidence and pretrained decision mechanisms. To address heterogeneous anomaly patterns, we construct complementary structural, attribute, and neighborhood evidence and transform heterogeneous statistics into graph-relative anomaly percentiles. To move beyond predefined numerical scoring rules, we leverage a single frozen pretrained language model for evidence-conditioned anomaly assessment. To bridge the semantic gap between numerical evidence and pretrained models, we design a semantic Graph-to-State (G2S) transformation that organizes graph context and semantically labeled node evidence into structured decision states for non-generative option-logit readout. The resulting decision scores are integrated with four complementary statistical scores through equal-weight rank-based fusion, without GAD-specific gradient-based optimization. Extensive experiments on seven graph anomaly detection benchmarks spanning citation, social, and co-review networks demonstrate the effectiveness of Jev-GAD, achieving average AUROC and AUPRC scores of 89.18\\% and 52.40\\%, respectively. a hybrid deep learning model with feature fusion attention and dual parallel CNN for drug-target binding affinity prediction","venue":"Journal of Supercomputing","year":2026},{"abstract":"Designing optimal auctions for allocating public infrastructure-such as airport slots and energy resources-is challenging due to interdependent resources and complex side-constraints. While the Vickrey-Clarke-Groves (VCG) auction guarantees maximum welfare, it cannot maximize revenue or accommodate the multi-objective trade-offs inherent in public infrastructure systems. We propose a differentiable, constraint-aware framework for combinatorial auction design that enables end-to-end learning of fractionally feasible, approximately strategy-proof mechanisms. Our primary contribution is a combinatorial constraint enforcement technique that ensures fractional feasibility by construction, bypassing the need for penalty-based approximations. We introduce CAGraph, a novel graph-based architecture designed to capture dependencies between items and bidders, alongside CANet and CAFormer as deep learning baselines, for combinatorial settings. We also provide a Matching Pursuit-inspired decomposition that maps fractional allocations to feasible discrete allocations and empirically evaluates the resulting discretization gap. In synthetic benchmarks and an airport slot-divestiture case study, respectively, the learned mechanisms achieve up to 73.5% and 180% higher expected revenue than VCG, under small empirical regret. Although RAG and Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) provide practical ways to enhance LLMs, they remain insufficient for temporal reasoning. To address these limitations, we propose Temporal Evidence-Parameter Co-Alignment (TEPCA), a framework for LLM reasoning over TKGs. TEPCA aligns LLM reasoning with temporal knowledge at both the evidence and parameter levels. At the evidence level, it introduces time-constrained Dynamic Relevance-Guided Path (DRGP) pruning to preserve globally coherent temporal paths, together with Mutual-Information (MI)-based pruning to retain query-informative local facts under temporal constraints. At the parameter level, it integrates Dynamic-Gated LoRA (DG-LoRA), a timestamp-conditioned low-rank adaptation mechanism that dynamically modulates the effective adaptation subspace according to temporal context. This design enables LLMs to better capture fine-grained entity evolution and time-dependent relation semantics while preserving parameter efficiency. Classical interior-point methods are robust and accurate, but their iterative nature can be costly in real-time or repeated-solve settings. This has motivated learning-based solvers that approximate optimizer solutions with neural networks. Recent work has increasingly studied graph neural networks (GNNs) for linear, quadratic, and second-order cone optimization, leveraging their ability to model sparse relational structure among variables, constraints, and objective functions. Most existing GNN-based solvers compress the optimization process into a single forward pass, predicting the optimizer directly without using the intermediate trajectory produced by classical solvers. We introduce SOCPNet, a recursive GNN framework that uses solver trajectories to learn an iterative SOCP solution procedure. A shared GNN model is applied repeatedly, refining the current iterate at each step and enabling inference for a variable number of iterations. Rather than predicting the solution in a single pass, SOCPNet learns from intermediate iterates to progressively refine its estimates using a trajectory-regularized training procedure. Real world transaction data for fraud detection is severely affected by class imbalance making it harder to detect these transactions. Fraudulent transactions are rarely isolated. However, conveying retrieved graphs through non-unique linear textual contexts to Large Language Models (LLMs) leads to graph-structure degradation and inefficient KV-cache reuse. However, existing methods face two key challenges when processing sports scenes: on one hand, target distribution in sports footage is strictly constrained by field boundaries, yet generic detectors uniformly allocate detection resources across the entire image, causing frequent false detections in off-field regions due to the visual similarity between spectators and athletes; on the other hand, objects such as athletes, balls, and referees in sports scenes form stable spatial co-occurrence patterns governed by game rules, yet existing methods predict each object independently, failing to leverage cross-category relational cues to assist the detection of difficult targets. To address these issues, this paper proposes SportRGDET (Sport Relation-Graph DEtection Transformer), a framework that achieves accurate detection through two core modules: the Scene Prior Guided Module (SPGM) jointly estimates the spatial probability distribution and boundary gradient map of the field region from multi-scale encoder features, fuses them to generate a hierarchical field confidence mask, and performs spatial modulation on the deformable self-attention weights of the encoder, which reallocates attention resources toward the effective field area and progressively suppresses off-field interference across layers, thereby reducing false detections while incurring only moderate additional computation; the Relation Reasoning Enhancement Module (RREM) treats each candidate object as a node during the detection decoding stage, adaptively learns inter-node association strengths through a relation encoder based on category embeddings and relative spatial positions of node pairs, constructs a dynamic relation graph, and bidirectionally propagates contextual information across nodes via graph attention mechanisms, enabling difficult targets to refine their predictions by leveraging positional and categorical cues from surrounding identified objects, enhancing detection robustness under occlusion and blur conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that SportRGDET achieves significant performance improvements on multiple sports detection benchmark datasets, validating the effectiveness of scene prior and relation reasoning mechanisms in sports scene object detection.","already_present":false,"authors":["Qing-Ya Ouyang","Chao-Yi Su","Qing-Yuan Li"],"candidate_id":"candidate-01b4abd2637fe5dd49f47842","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"doi":"10.1371/journal.pone.0348924","semantic_scholar":"aba7360477948d813a54f2a6d84e6e56fbebafa2"},"identity_key":"doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0348924","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/aba7360477948d813a54f2a6d84e6e56fbebafa2","title":"SportRGDET: Scene prior and relation graph enhanced detection transformer for sports scenes","venue":"PLoS ONE","year":2026},{"abstract":"Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) have demonstrated exceptional performance on graph-structured data. However, their success heavily relies on the availability of clean labels, an assumption that often fails in real-world scenarios. The learnability of GCNs is intrinsically linked to the neighborhood structure of nodes, making it critical to understand how this structure changes in the presence of label noise. In this work, we investigate how the neighborhood label distribution of a node changes under label noise. We mathematically derive that label noise smooths this distribution, which inherently increases its entropy and severely decreases interclass distinguishability. To address this challenge, we propose Leave-one-out Entropy Node Screening (LENS), an end-to-end framework that identifies noisy nodes by measuring the reduction in neighborhood entropy when a specific node is removed. LENS further incorporates a relabeling mechanism to recover and preserve valuable feature information instead of entirely discarding the identified noisy nodes. Crucially, the end-to-end computational overhead of LENS is remarkably low. To embed superpixels, current encoders crop them to bounding boxes and then pad, resize, or mask them, so background or fill values can leak into the node features. This matters in practice, and especially in medical imaging, where a prediction should depend on the tissue and not on an arbitrary preprocessing choice: on BACH, changing only the fill of the masked region shifts the accuracy of frozen encoders by up to 6 percentage points, larger than the differences among the four best encoders under mean fill, and the preferred fill differs between datasets, so it cannot be fixed once and for all. We present TAN (Tissue-Aware Network), a compact convolutional encoder (0.41M parameters) that processes each superpixel at its native shape and extent and excludes background from every operation, which makes its embeddings exactly invariant to the fill by construction. Under identical masks and an identical graph classifier, TAN's accuracy on BACH is not significantly different from that of the 303M-parameter foundation model UNI (81.1% vs. 80.7-82.6%, depending on the fill), with ~740x fewer parameters, ~1,190x fewer FLOPs, and no pretraining. On BRACS, TAN is close to a ResNet18 trained under the same protocol and trails the histopathology foundation models. An ablation with TAN's architecture but standard processing of fill-padded crops shows that masking keeps accuracy similar (nominally higher on BACH, lower on BRACS, within noise) at less than half the FLOPs.","already_present":false,"authors":["Jan Herschel","A. von Gladiss"],"candidate_id":"candidate-982bfe400a683d3b22e684c2","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.23475","semantic_scholar":"886d28e9d078a546083945e7c9dc3196c9966cf7"},"identity_key":"arxiv:2610.23475","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/886d28e9d078a546083945e7c9dc3196c9966cf7","title":"TAN: A Size- and Form-Adaptive Masked-Convolution Encoder for Tissue Graphs","venue":null,"year":2026},{"abstract":"Train delay heterogeneity between service categories is well known but rarely characterized at large scale from operational data, and rarely used directly to drive the design of graph-based delay-propagation models. This study uses the real International Railway Network Dataset (IRD2025) – 2,678,291 operational records from 3,324 trains across 1,397 stations on the Italian railway network, January–June 2024 – to empirically characterize this delay heterogeneity and to motivate and evaluate a heterogeneous graph-based delay-prediction framework (HTW-STGN).\n \n \n \n Exploratory analysis is conducted on the full real IRD2025 dataset, rather than the smaller synthetic validation sample used in earlier work, to characterize delay heterogeneity across the seven Italian train service categories and to test the empirical assumptions – cross-category delay correlation, weather sensitivity and category-level delay ranking – that originally motivated the heterogeneous-edge design of HTW-STGN. HTW-STGN is implemented as a relation-aware graph-feature aggregation model, with heterogeneous edges (same-category/cross-category) grounded in real, physically observed infrastructure sharing and evaluated on a held-out June 2024 test set.\n \n \n \n Results confirm and correct earlier reported patterns: regional services (96.4% of all records) have lower delays than long-distance categories, the opposite of the result reported from the earlier synthetic sample; the weather effect is real but moderate rather than strongly multiplicative as earlier estimated; and cross-category delay correlation is consistently weak (r = −0.05 to 0.37) rather than the high correlation (up to 0.89) that had originally motivated the choice of heterogeneous graph edges. Only 4.6% of station-to-station links in the network are used by more than one train category, and this real infrastructure-sharing structure – rather than delay correlation – is used to root HTW-STGN's heterogeneous edges. This design reduces mean absolute delay-prediction error by 12% beyond a homogeneous-graph baseline (95% CI [0.49, 0.63] min, p < 0.001) and by approximately 40% beyond features that ignore graph structure entirely, consistently across all seven categories.\n \n \n \n This is the first large-scale empirical characterization of delay heterogeneity across the full real Italian Railway Network Dataset, and the first to test – and correct – the correlational assumptions behind a heterogeneous graph-based delay-propagation architecture using real operational data rather than a synthetic proxy. Graph neural networks (GNNs) rely on message passing over these edges, making relational privacy protection a critical concern. To mitigate privacy risks, edge-level differential privacy (DP) has been widely adopted to perturb graph structures. However, existing edge-level DP mechanisms apply uniform perturbation across all edges, disregarding their heterogeneous structural importance. To address this limitation, we propose a personalized edge-level privacy-preserving GNN (PELP-GNN) learning framework, the first personalized edge-level privacy-preserving GNN learning framework, whose key novelty is to assign each edge a differentiated privacy budget according to its structural significance, thereby avoiding the overprotection of low-importance edges and the underprotection of critical ones. Specifically, PELP-GNN estimates edge importance based on forest edge centrality (FEC) and allocates personalized privacy budgets accordingly. Furthermore, it incorporates an adaptive aggregation scheme to mitigate the effects of nonuniform noise during message passing. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that PELP-GNN satisfies $\\epsilon $ -edge local DP (LDP) while providing personalized protection. Unlike existing works, PELP-GNN is a general, plug-and-play framework that can be seamlessly integrated into state-of-the-art edge-level DP-based GNN learning frameworks. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in accuracy across varying privacy budgets.","already_present":false,"authors":["Zi-Jun Song","Dian Lei","Yan-Li Yuan","Lie-Huang Zhu"],"candidate_id":"candidate-23f5d8307d957e5da1d08b7c","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"doi":"10.1109/jiot.2026.3721975","semantic_scholar":"0dab363602973fe3d7a9d49f3f2f47a6dd9694e4"},"identity_key":"doi:10.1109/jiot.2026.3721975","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/0dab363602973fe3d7a9d49f3f2f47a6dd9694e4","title":"Achieving Personalized Edge-Level Privacy-Preserving Graph Neural Networks on Decentralized Graphs","venue":"IEEE Internet of Things Journal","year":2026},{"abstract":"Cooperative localization (CL) is a key enabler for future cooperative intelligent transportation system applications. By sharing and fusing multisource information, it can provide high-accuracy localization for connected autonomous vehicles in GNSS-denied or limited environments. Practical CL scenarios often involve heterogeneous cooperative nodes, such as vehicles and landmarks, and relative measurements (e.g., range and bearing). However, existing graph neural network (GNN)-based CL methods do not sufficiently account for scene heterogeneity or fully exploit relative information. Moreover, the state components estimated in CL exhibit substantial scale discrepancies, making effective joint optimization crucial for improving the overall estimation performance of the model. To address these issues, a heterogeneous CL Graph Transformer (HCLGT), together with an adaptive optimization strategy, is proposed for the real-vehicle CL task. First, we incorporate edge-based relative position encoding into the attention computation to better leverage relative measurements. Second, we design relation-specific aggregation modules for different measurement relationships and employ node uncertainty to adaptively adjust attention weights, improving robustness under heterogeneous information quality. Finally, an adaptive loss function is developed to dynamically balance the optimization of multiscale state components. The proposed method is validated on the real-world Leibniz University Cooperative Perception and Urban Navigation Dataset (LUCOOP). Experimental results show that, compared with the best-performing baseline, the proposed method reduces the localization RMSE by 44.61%. Extensive experimental analyses further validate the effectiveness of each module.","already_present":false,"authors":["Sheng-Sheng Xing","Hai-Gen Min","Xia Wu","Wu-Qi Wang","Xiang-Mo Zhao","Guo-Qiang Mao"],"candidate_id":"candidate-1759d0ab90fd511ada8523ff","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"doi":"10.1109/jiot.2026.3720786","semantic_scholar":"dc5cc46d1ade8958a153b1c27d278a58760b3dbe"},"identity_key":"doi:10.1109/jiot.2026.3720786","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/dc5cc46d1ade8958a153b1c27d278a58760b3dbe","title":"Heterogeneous Graph Transformer for Connected Autonomous Vehicles' Cooperative Localization","venue":"IEEE Internet of Things Journal","year":2026},{"abstract":"Longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs) contain complementary diagnostic and laboratory information about patient health. However, irregularity, sparsity, heterogeneity, and incompleteness in documentation complicate EHR modeling. To address the problem, we introduce GraphBEAT (Graph-based Bucketized Event Aggregation over Time), a temporal graph representation learning framework that groups clinical events into time buckets and transforms observed features into patient-specific, temporally directed graphs to enable early risk stratification for gastrointestinal cancers. Each node in an EHR graph encodes feature identity, observed value, and temporal position of clinical events. A context-aware, time-decay message-passing mechanism models transitions between successive buckets, followed by multi-head attention pooling to generate patient-level representations. GraphBEAT was trained and evaluated on multi-site longitudinal diagnosis codes and laboratory tests to predict pancreatic, liver, and intestinal cancer at 12-, 24-, and 36-month diagnostic lead times. In all experimental setups, GraphBEAT consistently outperformed baseline graph neural networks (GraphSAGE, GAT, and GCN) and sequence modeling approaches (Transformer and long short-term memory [LSTM]). GraphBEAT also required over 250x fewer floating-point operations per patient and over 20x fewer parameters than the Transformer and LSTM baselines. These results support GraphBEAT as an accurate and computationally efficient approach for cancer risk stratification from sparse, heterogeneous longitudinal health records.","already_present":false,"authors":["L. Their size, however, targets data-centre inference, whereas low-inertia operation increasingly asks for inference at the edge, next to the measurement, at batch size one and within a single synchrophasor (PMU) reporting frame. We distil a 20.1M-parameter, 12-layer GridFM teacher into a 0.62M-parameter, 6-layer student, a $32.5\\times$ parameter reduction at half the message-passing depth, using an objective that combines the masked power-flow loss with output, physics-residual, latent-state and attention transfer. The physics-residual term, which matches the teacher's power-residual profile, has not previously been applied to typed power-grid graphs. We evaluate on a renewable variant of the IEEE 118-bus benchmark grid in which 26 of the conventional (synchronous) generators are replaced by inverter-based renewables with battery flexibility and standardised reactive-power limits (IEEE 1547), giving $97\\,529$ physically valid (AC-OPF-feasible) operating scenarios, and we ablate all eight combinations of the transfer terms, reporting accuracy against ground truth and fidelity to the teacher separately. Distillation lowers student error on all four predicted quantities, by up to $48\\%$ on active-power dispatch, and every distilled student is more accurate than its teacher on reactive-power dispatch. The gain is largely carried by the output matching term. The physics-residual term, in the layer-aggregated form used here, is consistently harmful, which we attribute to the spatial averaging it applies to a bus-level residual field. The resulting student is $32.5\\times$ smaller in parameter count and has half the message-passing depth, making it a candidate for subsequent edge-device benchmarking.","already_present":false,"authors":["Vlad Sanduleac","Shahariya Rasheed Rayamarakkarveettil Puthanpurayil","Noman Khan","R. Teodorescu"],"candidate_id":"candidate-095ed2123891e867cce0baff","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.21833","semantic_scholar":"327773d82d16c35f9676a063b1c475fb8f49b7e0"},"identity_key":"arxiv:2610.21833","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/327773d82d16c35f9676a063b1c475fb8f49b7e0","title":"Physics-Aware Distillation of a Grid Foundation Model for Real-Time Edge Inference","venue":null,"year":2026},{"abstract":"Mobile apps have become ubiquitous in daily life. Despite communication encryption, app fingerprinting (AF) attacks can still enable adversaries to infer the apps in use by analyzing patterns of encrypted network traffic. However, existing AF attacks suffer from three critical limitations that hinder their practical effectiveness: (i) the inability to capture app-specific traffic dependencies, rendering traffic fingerprints fragile under dynamic networking conditions; (ii) the neglect of latency and throughput considerations, resulting in inefficient real-time user tracking; and (iii) the incapacity to handle mixed traffic generated by multi-app concurrency. In this paper, we propose MAppPrint, a robust and real-time app fingerprinting framework. MAppPrint introduces a behavior-level traffic fingerprint, i.e., Traffic Behavior Correlation Graph (TBCG), which models app traffic by capturing unit traffic behaviors and their correlations, thereby providing reliable app fingerprints. To enable real-time fingerprinting, MAppPrint incorporates a fingerprint compression algorithm that transforms each TBCG into a compact graph by selectively aggregating redundant information. Furthermore, MAppPrint employs an unsupervised decomposition strategy to disentangle mixed traffic generated by multi-app concurrency, enabling unified identification of both single-app and multi-app traffic. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that MAppPrint achieves 4.9~13.9% improvement in AF precision and 3~6 times improvement in timeliness over state-of-the-art methods. Meanwhile, MAppPrint is robust in dynamic networking conditions, while achieving a throughput of 10.5 GB/s and a prediction latency of 0.68 seconds.","already_present":false,"authors":["Tao Duan","Jun-Zhou Zhao","Jiang-Long Li","Rong-Hua Li","Youqian Zhang","Nuo Xu","Ping-Hui Wang","Hai-Bo Hu"],"candidate_id":"candidate-cad8432d4c0d3786b2b76f68","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.22148","semantic_scholar":"037546eb64d981ac1bc8401ea4d9fa524a7d3722"},"identity_key":"arxiv:2610.22148","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/037546eb64d981ac1bc8401ea4d9fa524a7d3722","title":"MAppPrint: Robust and Real-time Mobile App Fingerprinting via Traffic Behavior Correlation Graphs","venue":null,"year":2026},{"abstract":"Sheaf neural networks generalize graph neural networks by assigning each edge a learned linear restriction map that specifies how the local representations of adjacent nodes relate to one another, thereby mitigating oversmoothing. Existing sheaf architectures, however, define the sheaf Laplacian as an instantaneous spatial operator and therefore cannot explicitly model how signals evolve over time on a graph. We first introduce a spectral sheaf Laplacian, defined jointly over space and time, such that a single operator regulates signal propagation across both the spatial graph and the temporal domain. Directly extending this operator's receptive field in space or time would require increasingly complex sheaf structures. Instead, we propose a spectral filter that expands the effective receptive field along both dimensions without enlarging the underlying sheaf. Building on this operator, we introduce ChronoSheaf, a spatio-temporal sheaf network with two key components. First, Transitional Restriction Maps (TRM) decompose each node's restriction map into a spatial term and two temporal frames that independently control its relation to neighboring nodes at the preceding and following timestep, enabling asymmetric temporal influence. Second, the Dual Spectral Filter (DSF) applies a single bounded-degree polynomial filter with an adaptively estimated spectral radius to the joint spatio-temporal sheaf operator. We validate ChronoSheaf on a diverse set of spatio-temporal forecasting benchmarks, where it outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/ChronoSheaf-1D7D/.","already_present":false,"authors":["A. Firstly, based on the data set related to education finance published by the Education Economics Laboratory, a heterogeneous graph modeling mechanism is designed to reconstruct the relationship between multiple node types, including teachers, courses, funds and outputs, and form a dynamic knowledge graph sequence. Secondly, by combining the Graph Attention Network (GAT) with the transformer architecture, a cross-time and cross-type performance cost representation model is constructed to support the teaching expenditure prediction and performance fitting analysis. Finally, an anomaly detection mechanism combining Autoencoder and Local Outlier Factor (AE + LOF) is introduced, and a closed-loop system is formed by optimizing budget allocation based on reinforcement learning strategy network. The results show that the prediction accuracy of the GAT model is better than that of the four baseline methods. In the annual scenario, the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) are reduced by 1.52% and 1.63% respectively, which has stronger error stability. In anomaly detection, the average F1 score of AE + LOF framework reaches 0.907, the false positive rate is controlled within 4.3%, and the sample fluctuation of adaptive institutions is less than 3.6%. In budget optimization experiments, the reinforcement learning policy achieved a ΔPerf/ΔCost of 0.178, with a performance improvement rate of 21.5% under high-performance preference conditions. System tests showed end-to-end latency below 200 ms and self-learning convergence within 18 epochs, with the highest user satisfaction rating in “interactivity.” Under the constraints of the data and simulation conditions of this study, graph-structured modeling and intelligent embedding mechanisms hold the potential to enhance the level of intelligence in performance-based cost accounting.","already_present":false,"authors":["An-Qi Jia","Yuan Chao","Liao-Wang Zou","Wei Liu"],"candidate_id":"candidate-e791f69ddefa8ac04f387561","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"doi":"10.1007/s10791-026-10598-9","semantic_scholar":"3543311c2317a8d52bd6542529f774b2a9b3efd9"},"identity_key":"doi:10.1007/s10791-026-10598-9","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/3543311c2317a8d52bd6542529f774b2a9b3efd9","title":"The analysis of intelligent university performance cost accounting driven by big data","venue":"Discover Computing","year":2026},{"abstract":"Resting-state functional connectivity is widely used in machine learning-based classification of neuropsychiatric disorders. Quantum machine learning models have been proposed for functional connectivity data, but few studies have evaluated them under leave-site-out validation or against matched classical models. We compared six quantum model families with classical ones using identical correlation-derived features across four public cohorts (4,308 subjects). Leave-site-out validation was used for the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE I), ADHD-200 (attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder), and REST-meta-MDD (major depressive disorder) cohorts, while the UCLA Consortium for Neuropsychiatric Phenomics (UCLA-CNP) was evaluated using stratified 10-fold cross-validation. The quantum kernel was statistically indistinguishable from a matched classical kernel across all four cohorts, with the average accuracy difference within 1.4 percentage points at 95% confidence. On ABIDE I, a hybrid quantum convolutional network achieved similar accuracy to its classical counterpart (0.645 vs. 0.641), while a trainable quantum kernel exceeded its classical counterpart by 0.064 in area under the curve (AUC). Quantum convolutional networks also achieved higher AUC than their matched classical networks on this cohort and showed smaller train-test gaps on all four cohorts, without an accuracy gain. Overall, most quantum models matched their classical counterparts, but none consistently outperformed them. This study, among the first quantum evaluations of ABIDE I under leave-site-out validation, provides a feature-matched benchmark of quantum and classical models comprising 284 matched comparisons. We further analyse fidelity-based graph construction and account for the observed quantum-classical parity through effective-dimension and eigenspectrum analyses.","already_present":false,"authors":["Utsav Poudel","Anuj Nepal","V. It is a disease with an often asymptomatic onset, which means that a high percentage of affected individuals remain unidentified until quite far in the disease process, thereby underlining the importance of a good, reliable screening instrument for proactive detection. In this paper, GlucoSense is introduced as a single framework for early NIDDM risk stratification by combining Human Activity Recognition (HAR) with continuous blood glucose forecasting using two Graph Attention Network version 2 (GATv2)-based architectures. The first is a HAR module trained with smartphone triaxial accelerometer data that covers 23 activity classes, while the second is a glucose prediction module trained with the OhioT1DM dataset to predict glucose levels for a 30 min horizon. The study was longitudinal, spanning 90 days, with six participants. The system was able to correctly identify metabolically healthy individuals and those with prediabetic patterns. The framework was cross-validated with HbA1c laboratory tests to verify the clinical consistency of the framework. Both modules were benchmarked against sequential, convolutional, attention-based, and graph-based baselines under an identical protocol with five independent runs. However, recent studies have revealed their vulnerability to adversarial attacks, where imperceptible perturbations to the graph structure can easily mislead predictions. Existing defense methods predominantly rely on global heuristic strategies, which often lead to over-smoothing in deep architectures and fail to capture localized, fine-grained structural anomalies. In this paper, we propose Topology-Aware Dynamic Co-evolution (TADC), a novel framework that reformulates graph defense as a closed-loop optimization process. Unlike static purification paradigms, TADC introduces a closed-loop dynamic co-evolution framework, in which graph topology and model parameters are jointly optimized through validation-guided meta-gradients, enabling continuous and adaptive structural refinement during training. To further ensure the reliability of topology updates, we identify the topology-agnostic limitation of conventional meta-gradients and propose a topology-aware gradient calibration mechanism, which incorporates structural priors to guide gradient directions toward more plausible and semantically consistent graph modifications. Concretely, TADC first localizes vulnerable nodes via a structural-semantic consistency probe and constructs an initialized graph through topology-aware refinement. It then performs structure decoupling to disentangle reliable and potentially adversarial edges into distinct channels. Building upon this decomposition, a fully differentiable attention-based architecture DeepGCN enables end-to-end optimization of the co-evolution process. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that TADC consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across various attack settings, with particularly pronounced advantages under strong adversarial perturbations and high perturbation rates. Under the message-passing framework, mainstream GNN models alternate between feature transformation and neighborhood aggregation. Fusing these two phases into a node-level pipelined push dataflow, in which each node’s transformed feature streams directly into aggregation, establishes a single-pass I/O target that reads each input tensor exactly once per layer. No existing hardware sustains this dataflow at full concurrency. Prior fusion accelerators fall short of this target in three ways: designs that gather the raw input features for aggregation or write transformed features off-chip incur redundant traffic, designs that stream transformed features on-chip still keep the two phases as separate matrix kernels without a unified execution granularity, and the designs that aggregate at message granularity serialize per-destination aggregation or allocate state that does not scale to large graphs. We propose PipeGNN, a bandwidth-efficient GNN accelerator whose streaming microarchitecture sustains this dataflow as a fully concurrent pipeline within a fixed on-chip buffer budget. PipeGNN decouples execution from topological boundaries by aligning execution granularity with both memory burst size and aggregation compute throughput, and resolves four coupled microarchitectural barriers through coordinated mechanisms: compute-aligned edge batching, contention-aware message reduction, adaptive cross-batch scheduling, and tiered state residency. Qualitative analysis shows the graph resolving errors that per-label scoring cannot, selecting a narrower gold descriptor where an unstructured re-ranker settles for its broader parent.","already_present":false,"authors":["Lakshmi Rajendram Bashyam"],"candidate_id":"candidate-9d56a14023cf9a9092fb212c","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.20048","doi":"10.1145/3805696.3846044","semantic_scholar":"2235eff7d497d10f077e66eb3b577e8a9b9eea7f"},"identity_key":"doi:10.1145/3805696.3846044","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/2235eff7d497d10f077e66eb3b577e8a9b9eea7f","title":"Reading the neighborhood: Text-Attentive Graph Reranking for Automated Subject Indexing","venue":"Proceedings of the 26th ACM/IEEE Joint Conference on Digital Libraries","year":2026},{"abstract":"With the widespread adoption of online social networks, social recommender systems have become a key paradigm for mitigating data sparsity and cold-start issues in traditional collaborative filtering. However, existing graph neural network (GNN) based recommendation models face two fundamental structural bottlenecks when dealing with real-world social data: social noise and over-smoothing. Invalid or weak social connections dilute preference signals, while representation homogenization induced by deep graph convolution undermines personalized recommendation. To address these challenges, this report proposes a new framework named SRIGB (Social Recommendation via Information Graph Bottleneck). SRIGB introduces the Information Bottleneck principle as a principled denoising mechanism by maximizing the mutual information between the denoised graph and interaction labels while minimizing redundant information with respect to the original noisy graph, thereby extracting task-relevant social structure more precisely. In addition, SRIGB incorporates a contrastive learning paradigm to counteract the smoothing effect of graph convolution, enabling the model to preserve high-order social influence while maintaining discriminative and independent user representations. This report presents the theoretical foundations, model architecture, and experimental design of SRIGB, aiming to provide both theoretical support and a practical technical pathway for building the next generation of robust social recommender systems.","already_present":false,"authors":["Jia-Lei Zhu","Yun-Long Song","Hong-Yun Zhang"],"candidate_id":"candidate-e6d5c459d857fee8bfd4c43e","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"doi":"10.1007/s10791-026-10640-w","semantic_scholar":"0c6f002c66a1c8a1d1b53e8bd92b1e8a0c22047f"},"identity_key":"doi:10.1007/s10791-026-10640-w","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/0c6f002c66a1c8a1d1b53e8bd92b1e8a0c22047f","title":"Sparsity-aware social recommendation via information graph bottleneck","venue":"Discover Computing","year":2026},{"abstract":"Entities in real-world systems often evolve over time: users shift between information consumption patterns, researchers migrate between fields, and firms transition between financial risk states. When such systems are modeled as dynamic graphs, these transitions correspond to nodes whose class labels change between consecutive snapshots, which we call shifters. Correctly classifying shifters is often more consequential than classifying stable nodes with persistent labels, as detecting such transitions enables timely intervention in high-stakes settings. Yet, we identify a systematic failure mode across all major dynamic graph neural network architectures: shifter performance consistently lags behind stable nodes, with errors concentrated on the old label. Our structural analysis traces this failure to embedding inertia: neighborhood aggregation keeps shifter representations anchored to the old-class centroid, and this effect is strongest precisely where it is hardest to correct, namely for shifters whose neighborhoods remain aligned with the old class. Guided by this finding, we propose CHASE, a model-agnostic CHange-Aware framework for Shifting nodEs that wraps any dynamic GNN with targeted components for detecting label shifts and overriding stale neighborhood signals. CHASE consistently improves shifter performance across all tested models and datasets (up to 114.9% and 202.5% improvement on accuracy and F1 score, respectively) while preserving stable-node performance. We additionally contribute three dynamic graph benchmarks with naturally shifting labels, filling a gap in existing resources. The source code is available at https://github.com/jhkim611/CHASE","already_present":false,"authors":["Junghoon Kim","Seungyoon Choi","Hyunsung Kim","Chanyoung Park"],"candidate_id":"candidate-c82234bc4ec215df07f7be32","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.17582","semantic_scholar":"84ea87d654aef1dde18ea31ef92c4fe4d2aec0df"},"identity_key":"arxiv:2610.17582","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/84ea87d654aef1dde18ea31ef92c4fe4d2aec0df","title":"Chasing Label Shifters: A Change-Aware Framework for Dynamic Graph Node Classification","venue":null,"year":2026},{"abstract":"Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) commonly assume that node features are fully observed, despite missing features being pervasive in real-world applications. By leveraging the dependence between node features and graph structure, existing graph-specific methods handle missingness by propagating observed feature values along graph edges. However, these methods have mainly been evaluated in overly optimistic settings, where feature entries are removed independently and uniformly across the graph. This overlooks realistic scenarios in which missingness propagates among connected nodes, as can occur during localized sensing failures in sensor networks. We formalize this complementary notion as graph-structured mask dependence, where the joint distribution of missingness indicators is shaped by the graph, and introduce a controlled mechanism that instantiates this setting. With zero labels, CB-RBM achieves AUROC>= 0.96 on four adversarial attacks and keeps FPR close to its calibrated 5% target under drift -- outperforming supervised GNNs (hundreds of labels), unsupervised graph-anomaly baselines, and a standard RBM whose FPR collapses to 89-100%. This study assesses the performance of six text-based models and a graph neural network (GNN) in mitigating the effects of misinformation using predefined social noise constructs. The dataset consists of 500,000 tweets collected from the X platform using the Ukraine hashtag during the Russia-Ukraine conflict from March 2024 to March 2025. Advanced machine learning models achieve strong performance, with accuracies ranging from 79.94% to 97.17%. RoBERTa demonstrates the highest performance, with an accuracy of 97.17%, Cohen's kappa of 0.9660, MCC of 0.9660, and AUC of 0.9977. The findings highlight that integrating social noise into AI pipelines enhances misinformation detection and supports more effective mitigation strategies in large-scale social media environments.","already_present":false,"authors":["Manar Alsaid"],"candidate_id":"candidate-258308376f684bb89849d84c","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.17469","semantic_scholar":"b2a7b79e467b5592c2a476d8f9016d0c8a715514"},"identity_key":"arxiv:2610.17469","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/b2a7b79e467b5592c2a476d8f9016d0c8a715514","title":"Assessing the Performance of AI Models in Misinformation Detection Using Predefined Social Noise Constructs","venue":null,"year":2026},{"abstract":"Online platforms often expose activity signals even when records of the underlying connections are incomplete or delayed. These activity responses may retain indirect evidence of connections that formed during the observation period but are absent from the recorded topology. Recovering such hidden structural changes can help keep network records aligned with evolving interactions and support downstream network analysis. However, the effects of a change propagate through the network and may overlap, making state changes difficult to associate with specific connections. We propose the Hierarchical Structural Context Ranker (HSCR), which combines visible network structure with node-state changes to infer connections that have formed but remain unrecorded. By jointly modeling the topological context of state responses and associations among potential connections, HSCR converts distributed activity changes into evidence for distinguishing potential connections without prespecified dynamical equations or parameters. Experiments on five temporal-network benchmarks and a real temporal Reddit network validate its effectiveness. Across observation spans and structural-record delays, true added connections achieve a 36%-50% reduction in mean true rank relative to the corresponding best baselines. This work provides a principled way to prioritize unrecorded additions for structural verification and record maintenance in online communities, information networks, and other networked systems.","already_present":false,"authors":["En Xu","Jing-Tao Ding","Yong Li"],"candidate_id":"candidate-69bd4315053b8ba0ec4c5593","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.16934","semantic_scholar":"5d78e27adf26560160f247d4d2fd66e51ce3c782"},"identity_key":"arxiv:2610.16934","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/5d78e27adf26560160f247d4d2fd66e51ce3c782","title":"Inferring Hidden Structural Changes from Node-State Responses under Partial Network Observations","venue":null,"year":2026},{"abstract":"Multimodal entity alignment (MMEA) is fundamental to integrating heterogeneous knowledge graphs (KGs), yet existing paradigms remain critically vulnerable to incomplete modalities and cross-graph structural asymmetries. This paper exposes a fundamental oversight in current MMEA research: treating feature missingness and topological discrepancies as isolated preprocessing or denoising challenges, which overlooks their destructive coupling during multimodal fusion. We systematically formulate and evaluate two newly identified failure modes: 1) Detail Missing (DM)-induced overvaluation, where the absence of local modality details causes models to overemphasize uninformative, blurred representations; and 2) Context Imbalance (CI)-induced suppression, where topological discrepancies across KGs allow dense structural contexts to overwhelm weaker but highly discriminative modal signals, triggering high-level semantic drift. To break this cycle of degradation, we introduce ALMEA, a generative and calibration framework that establishes a bidirectional feedback loop between low-level feature reconstruction and high-level latent space alignment. Specifically, Cross-Modality Imputation (CMI) synthesizes missing modality details to mitigate overvaluation, while Latent Semantic Calibration (LSC) aligns cross-graph joint embeddings to suppress topology-driven semantic drift. Under sparse supervision, we develop Controlled Iterative Selection (CIS) to adaptively acquire representative and diverse pseudo-labeled pairs, optimizing latent calibration under constrained budgets. Extensive evaluations on standard benchmarks demonstrate that ALMEA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. At a 20% supervision rate, ALMEA yields substantial absolute improvements of up to 5.20% in MRR and 6.40% in Hits@1, maintaining robust gains across higher supervision thresholds.","already_present":false,"authors":["Xi-Zhe Zhang","Jing-Feng Zhang","Meng-Fen Chiang"],"candidate_id":"candidate-6570ba1ef5a582d0637ec24c","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.16106","semantic_scholar":"283d12f5025036b5ad23089904fe5462312fdd48"},"identity_key":"arxiv:2610.16106","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/283d12f5025036b5ad23089904fe5462312fdd48","title":"Silence and Noise: Resolving Suppression and Overvaluation in Multimodal Entity Alignment","venue":null,"year":2026},{"abstract":"The global semiconductor industry has become a strategic pillar of the digital economy and mainly supports the artificial intelligence technology, cloud computing, advanced manufacturing, and modern electronic devices. This research used the BACI international trade database. First, we analyze the structural evolution of the global semiconductor trade network and identify its major trading communities. This paper proposes a two-stage matching model based on graph attention networks (GAT) that fuses electrical, topological, and information and communication technology (ICT) features. The first stage employs GAT for wiring mode identification, achieving 91.7% accuracy. The second stage recommends optimal FA configurations through feature fusion with embedded ICT feasibility hard constraints, attaining 83.3% Top-1 matching accuracy. However, cross‐integration of structurally unpaired and underutilized morphomic datasets (e.g., Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)‐stained images), remains a bottleneck due to inherent differences in spot structures, feature dimensions, and cellular heterogeneities. Here, we present AgaeSMO, an adaptive graph auto‐encoder for versatile cross‐modality integration of both structurally paired and unpaired spatial multi‐omics data. AgaeSMO encodes each omics modality from a cell type‐aware KNN (k‐nearest neighbor) feature graph and a spatial adjacency graph, while leverages GATs (Graph Attention Networks) as the backbone to fuse modalities by learning joint representations through an attention‐weighted module. It specially fuses structurally unpaired modalities, which applies a morphological transformation strategy by designing a cross‐guidance alignment among modalities through graph cross‐attention learning. AgaeSMO is a powerful tool can effectively integrate diverse omics modalities with both paired and unpaired spot architectures. This paper proposes State-Intent-Aware Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Cooperative Driving under Imperfect V2X (SIGN-MAPPO) to address these challenges through three coordinated mechanisms. Each decision-eligible connected and automated vehicle (CAV) first reconstructs a receiver-specific traffic graph from its ego state and the peer-state records available to it, from which a shared graph-attention policy generates a raw Stop/Go intention augmented with predicted HV-intent features. CAV intentions are then exchanged through timestamped vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) messages, and a local conflict-aware arbitration layer converts each CAV's intention into a safe executable action despite potentially inconsistent peer information. In the principal Simulation of Urban MObility (SUMO) evaluation, SIGN-MAPPO achieves a 97.53% completion rate, a 0.10% collision rate, and a mean intersection traversal time of 35.28 s. The trained policy also remains robust under the evaluated communication-delay and packet-loss ranges, and cross-scenario tests show complete traffic clearance across the tested settings, though safety margins narrow under compound unpredictable HV behavior.","already_present":false,"authors":["Zi-De Fan","Jia-Hui Yuan","Kai-Xin Zhang","Jun-Hao Fan","Xiao-He Li","Yi-Ru Wang"],"candidate_id":"candidate-0771915f54137e750f9afad9","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.15577","semantic_scholar":"f5a7931735282f7c2f40e19b26590d2cffae09e4"},"identity_key":"arxiv:2610.15577","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/f5a7931735282f7c2f40e19b26590d2cffae09e4","title":"SIGN-MAPPO: State-Intent-Aware Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Cooperative Driving under Imperfect V2X","venue":null,"year":2026},{"abstract":"In practical engineering and scientific computing, a real physical system can be reduced to a boundary value problem, and the adequate boundary information to determine the interior spatial distribution and evolutionary state of the physical field can be solved with linear equations, alternatively, the the real physical problem can be treated with boundary problems with in adequate information problems in field of machine learning. This paper proposes a deep learning framework for the recovery of missing boundary information using an attention-guided graph neural network (GNN) surrogate. The framework extracts features from the physical information on the discretized boundary into a latent space, and the missing boundary quantities are then predicted by the network. Thus, the nonlinear mapping from known boundary quantities to missing boundary quantities is learned using a variational autoencoder (VAE) architecture, while an attention mechanism is incorporated to better model the correlations among different types of boundary information. Furthermore, the interior physical field can be reconstructed using the conventional boundary element method (BEM) integral formulation. The effectiveness of the GNN-BEM framework is evaluated using numerical examples of the two-dimensional Laplace and Poisson equations, which demonstrate good performance in reconstruction accuracy, local detail preservation, and model stability. The results show that GNN-BEM provides a feasible computational framework for boundary information recovery and fast interior physical field reconstruction for partial differential equations under complex boundary conditions.","already_present":false,"authors":["Rong-Ze Gao","Yu-Wei Wu","Xin-Ran Ji","Xing-Yu Ren"],"candidate_id":"candidate-16757789a470e063a94a7b30","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.15590","semantic_scholar":"29a78d805053b7e62b05378613715df62e99efcc"},"identity_key":"arxiv:2610.15590","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/29a78d805053b7e62b05378613715df62e99efcc","title":"An Attention-Guided Graph Neural Network Surrogate for Boundary Integral Computation in Physical Field Reconstruction","venue":null,"year":2026},{"abstract":"Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown strong potential for text-attributed graph learning by leveraging rich pre-trained knowledge and language understanding capabilities. Combining LLMs with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) offers a promising paradigm for expanding the modeling capabilities of graph learning. However, LLMs and GNNs follow distinct learning paradigms, leading to a pronounced mismatch between their knowledge spaces. Such discrepancies make effective knowledge fusion nontrivial. Moreover, existing methods often incur substantial additional computation for only limited performance gains. To address these challenges, we propose DeKoR, an efficient framework for GNN and LLM knowledge fusion. To enable selective knowledge fusion, an adaptive router learns how much each node should rely on each expert. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that DeKoR outperforms existing baselines on both node and subgraph classification, achieving superior effectiveness and efficiency.","already_present":false,"authors":["Pei-Yuan Li","Yong-Qi Huang","Ji-Tao Zhao","Di Jin","Dong-Xiao He"],"candidate_id":"candidate-88a0ef74f4d546923561a8de","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"arxiv":"2610.14710","semantic_scholar":"f9099b351840e1a557b1e61ca3b9f0b4c5667b48"},"identity_key":"arxiv:2610.14710","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/f9099b351840e1a557b1e61ca3b9f0b4c5667b48","title":"DeKoR: Decomposed Knowledge Routing for Efficient GNN--LLM Fusion","venue":null,"year":2026},{"abstract":"To evaluate whether a compact bidirectional state-space autoencoder improves joint classification of species, cell type, and disease state from single-nucleus RNA-sequencing profiles in heart failure (HF), while yielding interpretable gene attributions. Compact bidirectional state-space autoencoders can outperform substantially larger dense autoencoders for joint cardiac transcriptomic classification while reducing parameters. scHFBiMamba enables accurate multi-task prediction and hypothesis-generating gene-level interpretation. This issue exacerbates passenger waiting times, creates load imbalances between buses, and undermines service reliability. Reinforcement learning (RL) has proven highly effective for mitigating bus bunching and outperforms traditional model-based approaches. However, existing RL approaches require agents to continuously interact with the environment, which potentially disrupts the bus system before effective policies are learned. This paper proposes an Offline Graph-based Multi-agent Actor-Critic (Offline-GMAC) method that trains bus holding policies using only readily available logged GPS data collected during normal uncontrolled operations, thereby eliminating the need for disruptive online interaction or exploration. The method employs general graph neural networks for multi-agent credit assignment. A key innovation of our method is a data augmentation scheme that synthesizes unperformed holding actions from historical uncontrolled bus trajectories. The scheme exploits the equivalence between stochastic link travel time delays and deliberate holding interventions. Under mild assumptions, we prove that the 1-Wasserstein distance between synthesized and target state transition distributions is bounded above by a term that scales linearly with the standard deviation of link travel times plus a tunable synthesis-dependent term. Existing approaches frequently depend on pre-established trust relationships or side-channel information, which may not be available or reliable in realistic MRS deployments. We formulate this as seed-conditioned response ranking: given a perturbation at one seed node, ranking all other nodes by response strength. This is challenging when the model is given only the interaction topology, while the mechanism governing how perturbations propagate must be learned from data. We present VQIL (Visible Quantum Interference Learning), a trainable Szegedy quantum walk for seed-conditioned ranking. Edge weights, link phases, and per-node phase rotations are optimized end-to-end by backpropagation while the walk operator remains unitary throughout training. Node scores are obtained from a geometrically discounted coherent sum of quantum-walk amplitudes, enabling quantum interference before the final squared-norm readout. Because each learned parameter is attached to a named edge or node, the trained model provides directly inspectable hypotheses about the roles of individual graph components in the propagation mechanism. On AC power-flow perturbations over six transmission grids, with electrical parameters withheld from the model, VQIL improves Spearman rank correlation from 0.147 for the untrained walk to 0.831 and outperforms an identically trained random-walk model. On gene perturbation over five protein-protein interaction networks with Perturb-seq supervision, VQIL improves rank correlation from 0.171 to 0.620, outperforming the strongest learned classical and neural baselines. However, conventional graphs are inherently limited to pairwise connections and are less effective at representing group-wise coordination patterns in human motion, where multiple joints often act as a functional unit during complex movements such as swinging or throwing. Hypergraphs provide a natural alternative by allowing hyperedges to connect arbitrary numbers of joints and explicitly encode coordinated joint groups. We propose the Motion-Guided Channel-Wise Hypergraph Convolutional Network (MC-HGCN), which models skeleton sequences through a unified hypergraph structure with three complementary mechanisms. MC-HGCN first constructs anatomical body-part and cross-limb hyperedges to provide structural priors. A motion-guided modulation mechanism adaptively reweights the hypergraph incidence matrix according to per-frame joint motion intensity, dynamically emphasizing active joint groups. Furthermore, a channel-wise hyperedge learning module discovers distinct coordination patterns across feature channels, enabling feature-specific relational modeling. A residual pathway preserves fine-grained pairwise information to complement high-order hypergraph aggregation. Extensive experiments on NTU RGB+D 60 and NTU RGB+D 120 demonstrate that MC-HGCN achieves strong performance using only joint coordinates, with notable improvements on high-motion actions involving complex multi-joint coordination. The hazard level of urban patrol cases can be reflected by the urgency level and prioritizing high-urgency cases can help reduce potential risks to public safety. However, it remains challenging to assess the urgency level of urban patrol cases when reliable urgency labels are limited or unavailable. To address this problem, this paper proposes an urban patrol case urgency classification method based on self-supervised clustering of a graph neural network. First, a case-relationship graph is constructed from urban patrol cases. A graph attention-based autoencoder is then pretrained to learn node representations, and K-means is used to initialize cluster centers. Finally, representation learning and clustering are jointly optimized to identify urgency-oriented clusters without using manual labels during training. Experimental validation was conducted using 6126 urban patrol case records from Zhengzhou, China. The proposed method achieved a Recall of 0.7458, Precision of 0.7465, ACC of 0.7424, F1 of 0.7403, and NMI of 0.4517. Compared with TADW, the strongest baseline, the proposed method improved these metrics by 0.0617, 0.0479, 0.0650, 0.0690, and 0.0407, respectively. These results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively learn urgency-related latent representations and improve the classification quality of urban patrol cases.","already_present":false,"authors":["Yi-Rui Jiang","Hao Wu","Tie-Jun Yang","Jia-Yu Sun","Hong-Wei Li","Wen-Jie Zhu"],"candidate_id":"candidate-86fd684e23a2bf72f9dda4c7","catalog_paper_id":null,"citation_count":0,"external_ids":{"doi":"10.1371/journal.pone.0360432","semantic_scholar":"f6dfbbea43d29a2b7a5d15650a6448a6772825ec"},"identity_key":"doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0360432","keywords":[],"node_id":null,"provenance":{"operation":"search","provider":"semantic_scholar"},"relation":"citation","relation_source_node_id":"21041260a5394f42891b020128fa60fa","removed":false,"source_url":"https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/f6dfbbea43d29a2b7a5d15650a6448a6772825ec","title":"An urban patrol case urgency classification method based on self-supervised clustering of a graph neural network","venue":"PLoS ONE","year":2026},{"abstract":"The unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based maritime surveillance is becoming an important part of maritime Internet of Things (IoT) and intelligent transportation systems. It provides a flexible and cost-effective way to large-scale maritime traffic monitoring. However, achieving robust situational awareness remains challenging in practical maritime environments. The main challenges arise from heterogeneous sensing modalities, adverse imaging conditions, and spatial misalignment caused by UAV motion. To address these problems, this paper proposes an airborne multi-modal graph learning-driven framework, termed AMGT, for vessel identification and tracking in UAV-assisted maritime IoT. Specifically, visible and infrared images are first aligned and fused through a multi-parameter perspective transformation model. This improves visual perception under low visibility and complex illumination conditions. Automatic identification system (AIS) messages are then temporally synchronized using interpolation and linear prediction. To detect small and oriented vessels, we develop a mixed-modality MAir-YOLOv8-OBB detector, followed by the MAir-SORT algorithm for stable vessel tracking. We further design a graph learning-driven association network to model temporal dynamics and spatial dependencies among vessels and between vessels and UAVs. A motion-aware coordinate unification (MCU) strategy is also introduced to reduce nonlinear misalignment caused by UAV motion. Experiments on the MAP-M2UAV50 dataset show that AMGT achieves high accuracy and efficiency. The results demonstrate its potential for UAV-assisted maritime IoT applications, including vessel monitoring, traffic situational awareness, and intelligent maritime transportation services. Combined with the exchangeability requirement on the output distribution, the terminal prior is necessarily an Erd\\H{o}s--R\\'enyi (E-R) random graph. In practice, generated graphs fail to recover meaningful node heterogeneity and higher-order structure. Previous models introduced specialized node features to compensate, framing this as an expressivity problem, while the role of the prior remained unexamined. We instead address the root cause by introducing the Latent Sociability Prior (LSP) and a join} diffusion process that co-evolves latent node sociability variables and graph structure, removing edge independence while preserving exchangeability.
